title: Sustainability solutions consultant (french & german speaking)
description:
About Watershed

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

The role

We're looking for more early members to join our Sustainability solutions team! You may be a fit for this role if you’re excited to help Europe's largest companies deliver real decarbonisation, navigate an increasingly complex landscape of investor pressure, customer expectations and regulatory requirements. You’re willing to roll your sleeves up and go deep with prospective customers on their functional and technical needs, partnering with our sales, product and climate science teams along the way. You may be a carbon accounting aficionado or you may have never worked in climate before but have a passion for the subject; either way, you have a knack for quickly learning new, complex topics and distilling them for others.

You will: 

- Partner closely with 3-4 Account Executives, to analyse and understand customers’ businesses, climate ambitions and software needs

- Become a trusted advisor to our prospective customers—educating them about corporate climate commitments, carbon accounting, regulation/policy and the Watershed offering

- Build and share subject matter expertise on how the world’s largest companies can run successful climate programs

- Demonstrate Watershed’s unique value to prospective customers, through product demonstrations, ROI analysis and customer stories

- Creatively apply the Agentic AI capabilities of the Watershed platform to address innovative use cases

- Scope complex customer engagements as Watershed expands to new industries

- Interface with Customer Success and Sustainability Advisory teams to ensure smooth handovers from pre- to post-contract

- Collaborate with Watershed’s Engineering, Product and Marketing teams to continuously improve Watershed’s products and positioning

- It is a mandatory requirement to have business level French and German for this role 

You might be a fit if you: 

- Have worked in a Solutions Consulting or Sales Engineering role for an Enterprise SaaS company

- Have partnered with Account Executives to scope successful engagements with mid-sized to large companies

- Master new concepts and technologies quickly

- Have exceptional communication and presentation skills; can engage deeply with both technical and business executive audiences

- Get energy from working across multiple projects concurrently and wearing many hats

- Are passionate about decarbonising diverse industries, from aviation to manufacturing to cloud computing

- Are excited to join a startup and are ready to take responsibility defining a new standard for climate and Sustainability AI programs around the world!

Considered a “very nice to have” if you: 

- Have a background in corporate climate programs or carbon accounting

- Have policy experience, especially in climate/sustainability/corporate reporting

This role might include up to 25% travel.

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles) 

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.

What’s the interview process like? 

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

What if I need accommodations for my interview? 

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

Aufgaben

Du entwickelst easybill-mobile auf Basis von React Native, Expo und TypeScript für iOS und Android weiter. Eine technische Grundlage mit Anmeldung, Dashboard und Dokumentenübersichten ist bereits vorhanden. Darauf baust du auf und gestaltest die nächsten Schritte gemeinsam mit dem Team.

- Du nutzt KI-Werkzeuge wie Claude Code intensiv im Entwicklungsalltag und übernimmst Verantwortung für die Qualität, Verständlichkeit und Korrektheit der Ergebnisse.

Unser Mobile-Stack umfasst React Native, Expo, Expo Router und TypeScript. Dazu kommen TanStack Query und TanStack Form, Zod und NativeWind. Für Tests setzen wir auf Jest und React Native Testing Library. Unsere bestehende Plattform und die REST-API basieren auf PHP und Symfony.

Qualifikation

- Du musst nicht jede Bibliothek bereits kennen. Entscheidend ist, dass du deinen Stack verstehst, gute technische Entscheidungen triffst und dich selbstständig in neue Themen einarbeitest.

- Du hast fundierte Erfahrung mit TypeScript, React Native und Expo auf Senior-Level und hast mobile Anwendungen über die reine Implementierung hinaus bis zum Release begleitet.

- Du verstehst React, Komponentenarchitektur, Zustandsverwaltung und asynchrone Datenflüsse und kannst komplexe Zusammenhänge verständlich strukturieren.

- Du kennst die Besonderheiten von iOS und Android und gehst systematisch an Performance-Probleme, Plattformfehler und Debugging heran.

- Du bist sicher in der Anbindung von REST-APIs und verstehst API-Verträge, Authentifizierung, Validierung und Fehlerbehandlung.

- Idealerweise bringst du zusätzlich Kenntnisse in PHP und Symfony mit. Du kannst bestehende API-Endpunkte verstehen, Fehler zwischen App und Backend analysieren und Schnittstellen eigenständig erweitern.

- Du arbeitest eigenständig und pragmatisch, kommunizierst klar und behältst den Nutzen für unsere Kundinnen und Kunden im Blick.

- Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und hast gute Englischkenntnisse.

Wenn du nicht jedes Kästchen erfüllst, aber ein außergewöhnlich starker Engineer bist: Bewirb dich trotzdem und zeig uns, was du gebaut hast. Zeig uns, was du gebaut hast!

Benefits

title: Algorithm Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
What is Anori Tech doing?

The world talks about batteries, cells and the energy transition. Almost nobody talks about the Battery Management System (BMS) that makes them work.

As battery applications multiply, from robotics and mobility to data centers and grid-scale storage, BMS complexity is exploding. Legacy BMS architectures were never built for this: too rigid to keep up with new requirements, they've turned the BMS into the bottleneck of battery development.

We're building something different: a novel software-defined BMS architecture combined with an AI-driven configuration process. It gets battery manufacturers the right BMS for their exact use case within days, regardless of application or cell chemistry.

We're building the battery management system platform of tomorrow. Delivered in days, not years.

Join us and shape one of the fastest growing markets in the energy sector: The BMS market.

Our Motivation

At Anori Tech, we believe everything is energy, and progress runs on it. With Anori we actively shape the energy transition: from oil to electric, from low to high efficiency. We need batteries for this transition and almost all batteries need a BMS. We strive for Shenzhen speed and German engineering quality. Our objective: put Europe back on the map in the race for the energy transition and build technical leadership out of Hamburg.

About the Role

A BMS is only as good as what it knows about the battery. As our Algorithm Engineer, you'll develop the algorithms that tell the Anori BMS what is happening inside the cells: state of charge, state of health and balancing. And you won't stop at the concept: you'll design algorithms, implement them in our embedded Rust firmware and validate them on real hardware. Later on, the role grows into the cloud, where data pipelines and fleet analytics will build on the models you create today. You'll work closely with Stefan, our CTO, and our firmware and hardware engineers.

Start date : from January 1, 2027

What You'll Do

- Develop the algorithms that estimate SoC and SoH for different cell chemistries and applications

- Design balancing strategies that fit the hardware and use case

- Build battery models (e.g. equivalent circuit models) and parameterize them from measurement data with statistical rigor

The next step is turning the lab prototype into an automated instrument and deciding between licensing and starting a company — which is where a business co-founder comes in. - Turn the lab prototype (TRL 3-4) into an automated, sellable instrument in partnership with the technical team.

Requirements

Core experience

- Comfort making a licensing-vs-startup call and building a go-to-market plan from a lab-stage prototype.

Especially valuable

- ChillQuanta is separately seeking an AI/ML co-founder to build wafer-scale AI prediction — relevant ML/software experience is valuable for that parallel track.

Benefits

- A validated lab prototype (TRL 3-4) benchmarked against single-atom data, with an Invention Disclosure already accepted by RUB and a manuscript heading to Physical Review Letters.
- A genuinely novel technique (patent filing in progress) addressing a real gap in photonic-qubit inspection for the fast-growing quantum and semiconductor chip markets.
- Ground-floor business co-founder equity alongside a strong physics/chemistry founding team.

title: SAP Koordinator (m/w/d) – Schnittstellen, Berechtigungen & Dienstleistersteuerung
description:
Sie kennen SAP aus dem laufenden Betrieb, bis in Tabellen, Logs und Transporte?

Über unseren Mandanten

Unser Mandant ist ein international tätiger Industriezulieferer der Mobilitätsbranche mit Hauptsitz im Großraum Kassel. Das Unternehmen wächst auf einer sehr soliden Auftragsbasis, und die IT soll dieses Wachstum mit stabilen Systemen tragen.

Warum diese Rolle?

Das SAP-System läuft auf ECC 6.0, ist über Jahre gewachsen und soll auf S/4HANA umgestellt werden. Die Basis betreibt ein externer Dienstleister, in den Fachbereichen entsteht ein Key-User-Konzept. Gesucht wird die Person, die das Ganze technisch zusammenhält.

• Weil Sie die Verantwortung für ein SAP-Backend tragen, das zuverlässig läuft.

• Weil Sie den Weg von ECC zu S/4HANA von Anfang an begleiten.

• Weil Sie Zuständigkeiten klären und Strukturen schaffen, die bleiben.

Das sind Ihre Aufgaben

• Sie behalten Hintergrundjobs, IDoc-Verarbeitung, RFC-Verbindungen, EDI-Strecken und angebundene Drittsysteme im Blick. Fehler analysieren Sie über Dumps, Logs und Traces und verfolgen sie bis zur Lösung.

• Sie koordinieren den Basis-Dienstleister bei Upgrades, Patches und Performance-Themen, später auch beim Wechsel auf S/4HANA, und fordern Ergebnisse ein.

• Sie prüfen Anforderungen und legen fest, ob Sie selbst umsetzen, den Dienstleister beauftragen oder die Aufgabe an den Fachbereich geben.

• Sie unterstützen die Fachbereiche beim Aufbau ihrer Key-User-Rollen.

• Sie erledigen selbst Benutzer und Rollen, SAPscript- und Smartforms-Anpassungen, Jobeinplanung, Systemnachrichten und kleinere technische Änderungen.

• Sie halten Systemlandschaft und Abläufe schriftlich fest, sodass Wissen im Unternehmen bleibt.

Zur Einordnung: Installation, Datenbank und Betriebssystem verantwortet der Basis-Dienstleister. Sie steuern ihn und sind die Ansprechperson für alles im SAP-Umfeld, wofür es noch keine klare Zuständigkeit gibt.

Das bringen Sie mit

• Eine IT-nahe oder kaufmännische Ausbildung oder ein Studium

• Mehrere Jahre SAP-Erfahrung im Inhouse-Betrieb eines Unternehmens, idealerweise mit ECC 6.0

• Technischen Tiefgang: Sie lesen Dumps und Traces, kennen Jobs, Transporte und Tabellen und sprechen mit dem Basis-Dienstleister auf Augenhöhe

• Praxis mit IDocs, RFC und EDI sowie mit Rollen und Berechtigungen (PFCG, SU53)

• Erfahrung in Projekten und in der Steuerung externer Partner, dazu Ausdauer beim Nachhaken

• Sehr gutes Deutsch und gutes Englisch

• Von Vorteil: Erfahrung mit Middleware und erste Berührungspunkte mit S/4HANA

Das erwartet Sie

• Arbeitsplatz im Großraum Kassel: Die Rolle lebt vom direkten Austausch, deshalb arbeiten Sie überwiegend vor Ort

• Flexible Arbeitszeiten und 30 Tage Urlaub

• Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket, Bikeleasing und Weiterbildung

Interesse?

Wenn Sie sich in dieser Rolle wiederfinden, senden Sie uns Ihren Lebenslauf mit Gehaltsvorstellung und frühestem Eintrittstermin.

title: Founding Principal Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
About us

Most labs still count cells under a microscope by hand. It's slow, repetitive, and error-prone. We're replacing that manual work with software. By combining a standard microscope with a smartphone, we run computer vision models that locate, track, and measure cells automatically in real time. We're starting with semen analysis and expanding to other routine microscopic samples. We're a small, well-funded team in Berlin, founded in 2026. Our goal is to make automated, reliable diagnostic analysis accessible on any phone connected to a microscope.

The role

We're looking for an engineer who wants to own the whole platform behind a medical product: services, data, infrastructure, security and identity. A first version runs today. The hard part is making it trustworthy enough for clinical use: patient data that stays safe, an audit trail that holds up for years, and a system that recovers when something breaks. You'll own all of it, working closely with the founders and our CTO.

What you'll do

- Own the platform end to end: backend, data, infrastructure and security.

- Get it ready for clinical use, and keep it reliable as we grow.

- Build identity, access and data handling that clinics and auditors can trust.

- Make the architecture calls: what to build now, what to defer, what to cut.

- Set the engineering standard and help hire the team that follows.

What you bring

- Platforms you've built and run. You've built backend platforms from scratch and run them in production, through outages, data incidents, migrations and growth.

- Database depth. You know what happens under the query: indexing, locking, transactions, replication, zero-downtime schema changes, and backups you've actually restored.

- Security by default. Authentication and authorisation, tenant isolation, secrets, audit logging. You think about how a system gets attacked before it ships.

- Identity done properly. Identity providers, sessions and tokens, roles and permissions, onboarding and offboarding.

- Infrastructure. Infrastructure as code, containers, Linux, networking and cloud are everyday tools for you.

- Beyond the backend. The backend is your home, but when the product needs it, you read and change the app yourself.

- Systematic troubleshooting. You reproduce first and fix root causes. You work from evidence like logs, traces, metrics and query plans, and you stay calm when production breaks.

- AI-native engineering. Coding agents are part of your daily work. You give them good context, split work into reviewable steps, and stand behind every line you ship.

- Ownership. You help shape the roadmap, push back on weak ideas, set your own priorities and raise problems early. Nobody has to chase you. Strong opinions, held with evidence and open to revision.

- Range. You've worked across several companies, stacks or environments. How you work counts far more than how many years you've done it.

Nice to have

- Regulated environments with audits: medical devices, health, finance.

- Serving ML models in production.

What we offer

- Ownership from day one. As a founding engineer, you're part of the company through our virtual share option plan (VSOP).

- You grow with us. As the company grows, your role grows with it.

- Real influence. You decide how we build software, and you shape the engineering team we build.

- A competitive salary.

- A product that matters: a medical device for real clinics, built together with clinicians and lab staff.

- Flexible hours and office days. We work from Berlin and meet in person regularly, up to several days a week. This isn't a fully remote role.

- English is our working language. German isn't required.

- We sponsor the EU Blue Card if you're moving to Berlin.

By combining a standard microscope with a smartphone, we run computer vision models that locate, track, and measure cells automatically in real time. We're starting with semen analysis and expanding to other routine microscopic samples. We're a small, well-funded team in Berlin, founded in 2026. Our goal is to make automated, reliable diagnostic analysis accessible on any phone connected to a microscope.

The role

We're looking for an iOS engineer who loves the camera. Our app turns an iPhone on a microscope into a lab instrument, and the hard problems live on the device: holding focus on a moving sample, running computer vision in real time, and capturing a recording precise enough for a clinical result. On top of that, the app has to be simple enough for a technician in a busy lab. You'll own it end to end, together with the founders.

What you'll do

- Own the app end to end, from architecture to release.

- Push the iPhone camera and on-device models to their limits, so every recording is good enough to analyse.

- Design the capture workflow with lab staff, so technicians get it right the first time.

- Spend time in the lab, measure what works, and decide what to build next.

What you bring

- Camera depth. You've built on the iOS camera stack, not just used it: AVFoundation with manual focus, exposure and white balance, and real-time frame processing. You know where the hardware's limits are.

- On-device ML. You've run models on the phone and made them fast: Core ML and Vision, quantisation, the Neural Engine, profiling with Instruments.

- Apps you've owned. You've shipped iOS apps in Swift and SwiftUI and owned them in production. You design an architecture one engineer can carry, and you can explain the trade-offs behind it.

- Product and UX sense. You turn a messy real-world workflow into something simple, and you test it with the people who use it.

- Built for real conditions. Offline-first, background uploads, interruptions, data protection. The app works when the network doesn't.

- Beyond the app. iOS is your home, but when the app needs it, you read the backend and change an API yourself.

- Correctness. You validate with numbers, not by eye. Tests are part of the feature. You reproduce bugs first and fix the cause, not the symptom.

- AI-native engineering. Coding agents are part of your daily work. You give them good context, split work into reviewable steps, and stand behind every line you ship.

- Ownership. You help shape the roadmap, push back on weak ideas, set your own priorities and raise problems early. Nobody has to chase you.

- Range. You've worked across several companies, stacks or environments. How you work counts far more than how many years you've done it.

Nice to have

- Optics or microscopy imaging.

- Apps for professional users: lab, field, clinical or enterprise.

- Regulated environments with audits: medical devices, health, finance.

What we offer

- Ownership from day one. As a founding engineer, you're part of the company through our virtual share option plan (VSOP).

- You grow with us. As the company grows, your role grows with it.

- Real influence. You decide how we build software, and you shape the engineering team we build.

- A competitive salary.

- A product that matters: a medical device for real clinics, built together with clinicians and lab staff.

- Flexible hours and office days. We work from Berlin and meet in person regularly, up to several days a week. This isn't a fully remote role.

- English is our working language. German isn't required.

- We sponsor the EU Blue Card if you're moving to Berlin.

- Energie tanken: Kalte und warme Getränke sowie frisches Obst stehen dir kostenlos zur Verfügung.

- Mitgestalten statt nur mitarbeiten: Bringe deine Ideen ein und gestalte aktiv unsere gemeinsame Zukunft.

- Aus Fehlern lernen: Eine offene und positive Fehlerkultur sorgt für Vertrauen, Entwicklung und echtes Teamwork.

title: Praktikant (m/w/d) - Praktikum Marketing & Präsentationsgestaltung (m/w/d)
description:
Karriereservice,de steht für professionelle Karriereberatung, praxisnahe Führungstrainings und modernes Outplacement. Wir begleiten Menschen auf ihrem beruflichen Weg – ob beim Karriereeinstieg, in der Neuorientierung oder beim nächsten Karriereschritt. Unsere Kunden sind Unternehmen, Hochschulen und Privatpersonen.

Zur kreativen Unterstützung unseres Teams suchen wir Dich – in unserem Büro Kaarst, hybrid oder vollständig remote. Dein Schwerpunkt liegt auf der Erstellung und Gestaltung ansprechender Präsentationen. Darüber hinaus wirkst Du an Blogartikeln sowie weiteren Marketing- und Kommunikationsmaßnahmen mit und bringst eigene Ideen für unseren Außenauftritt ein.

Start & Dauer: Idealerweise startest Du im November oder Dezember und unterstützt uns für etwa drei Monate. Den genauen Zeitraum stimmen wir gerne gemeinsam mit Dir ab.

Aufgaben

Freue Dich auf die Arbeit in einem modernen und offenen Beratungsunternehmen. Bei uns bist Du von Anfang an mittendrin statt nur dabei und gestaltest aktiv mit. Dich erwarten abwechslungsreiche Aufgaben, Raum für eigene Ideen und Einblicke in unseren Beratungsalltag:

- Du gestaltest Präsentationen und Schulungsunterlagen rund um Karriere, Bewerbung, Persönlichkeitsentwicklung und Führung und bringst Inhalte verständlich und visuell ansprechend auf den Punkt.

- Du wirkst an Blogartikeln und weiteren Texten mit: Du recherchierst spannende Themen, entwickelst Ideen und unterstützt uns beim Schreiben und Überarbeiten.

- Du unterstützt unseren digitalen Auftritt mit Beiträgen, Grafiken und kreativen Konzepten für unsere Webseite und Social-Media-Kanäle wie LinkedIn und Instagram.

- Du gestaltest weitere Marketingmaterialien mit , wie beispielsweise die Vorstellung unserer Beratungs- und Trainingsangebote.

- Du arbeitest eng mit unserem Beraterteam und anderen Werkstudierenden zusammen , tauschst Ideen aus und setzt gemeinsame Projekte um.

- Du erhältst Einblicke in unser Unternehmen und unsere Arbeitsweise: Du lernst unterschiedliche Beratungs- und Trainingsangebote kennen und erfährst, wie wir Menschen bei ihrer beruflichen Entwicklung begleiten.

- Du bringst eigene Ideen ein und übernimmst Verantwortung für kleinere Projekte, passend zu Deinen Interessen und Stärken.

Qualifikation

Du studierst beispielsweise BWL mit Schwerpunkt Marketing, Kommunikations- oder Medienwissenschaften, Kommunikationsdesign, Grafikdesign oder ein vergleichbares Fach. Entscheidend sind für uns Dein Interesse an Marketing und Kommunikation sowie Deine Freude daran, Inhalte und Ideen ansprechend aufzubereiten.

Außerdem bringst Du Folgendes mit:

- Du hast ein Gespür für Gestaltung und Freude daran, Präsentationen, Grafiken und andere Materialien übersichtlich und ansprechend zu gestalten.

- Du formulierst klar und verständlich und hast Spaß daran, Texte zu entwickeln, zu überarbeiten und auf unterschiedliche Zielgruppen abzustimmen.

- Du interessierst Dich für Karriere, Arbeitswelt und Persönlichkeitsentwicklung und arbeitest Dich gerne in neue Themen ein.

- Du bist digital affin: Erste Erfahrungen mit PowerPoint, Canva oder vergleichbaren Gestaltungsprogrammen sind willkommen. Kenntnisse in Social Media oder der Webseitenpflege sind ein zusätzliches Plus.

- Du bist neugierig auf die Möglichkeiten von KI und möchtest sie für Recherche, Texte und Gestaltung sinnvoll einsetzen. Erste Erfahrungen sind willkommen. Vieles kannst Du auch bei uns lernen.

- Du arbeitest zuverlässig und zunehmend eigenständig , achtest auf Details und fragst nach, wenn Du Unterstützung brauchst.

- Du hast Lust auf Zusammenarbeit , tauschst Dich gerne mit unserem Beraterteam und anderen Werkstudierenden aus und bringst eigene Ideen ein.

Du musst noch nicht alles können. Wichtig ist, dass Du Lust hast, Neues auszuprobieren, dazuzulernen und gemeinsam mit uns etwas umzusetzen.

Benefits

Darauf kannst Du Dich freuen! 

- Mitgestalten von Anfang an: Du übernimmst eigene Aufgaben und Projekte und erhältst dabei Unterstützung aus dem Team.

- Abwechslung & Einblicke: Du probierst Dich aus und lernst unseren Beratungs- und Trainingsalltag kennen.

- Kreativer Freiraum: Deine Ideen sind willkommen. Du kannst neue Formate entwickeln und Deine Stärken einbringen.

- Flexibilität & Vertrauen: Arbeite in unserem Büro in Kaarst, hybrid oder vollständig remote – mit flexiblen Zeiten, die zu Deiner Lebenssituation passen.

- Zusammenarbeit auf Augenhöhe: Dich erwartet ein offenes Team mit persönlichem Austausch, Humor und gegenseitiger Unterstützung.

- Lernen & Weiterentwicklung: Du sammelst praktische Erfahrung, erhältst konstruktives Feedback und erweiterst Deine Kenntnisse in Gestaltung, Kommunikation und KI.

title: Director, Global Field Operations
description:
Who is Sonar? 

Sonar enables organizations to ship agentic code with confidence. Code creation is abundant, but confidence is scarce. Our core platform, SonarQube, verifies over 750 billion lines of code every day, delivering agentic verification and governance for all code. Trusted by more than 7 million developers and 75% of the Fortune 100, including teams at Nvidia, ServiceNow, Booking.com , Goldman Sachs, AstraZeneca, and Ford Motor Company, Sonar enables organizations to reduce outages, improve security, and lower the cost and risk of agentic software development.

Founded in Geneva and now headquartered in Austin, Texas, Sonar has a global team working across offices and hubs, including Silicon Valley, London, Bochum, Barcelona, Singapore, Tokyo, and the Washington, D.C. area. At Sonar, we’re enabling enterprises to build agentic software factories that can move quickly while maintaining the control, consistency and evidence required to ship with confidence. 

Position description 

Sonar is scaling its go-to-market engine across Sales, Customer Success, and post-sales teams in every region. As the company grows, the field needs operating changes that are consistent, measurable, and adopted, not a collection of regional fixes. This role exists to design, land, and measure those changes.

As Director, Global Field Operations, you will sit in Revenue Operations as an individual contributor at Principal level, dedicated 100% to global field operations initiatives. You will not carry a regional support remit. You will own the portfolio of initiatives that change how the global field plans, sells, forecasts, and retains customers, from problem definition through rollout to measured business impact. You will be judged on outcomes such as conversion, pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy, productivity, and retention, not on the volume of activity delivered.

What You'll Do 

- 
Own a portfolio of global field initiatives end to end: problem definition, business case, design, rollout, and post-launch review. Prioritise on expected impact and effort, and stop or pivot initiatives that are not moving their target metric.

- 
Define the baseline, target, KPI, and owner for every initiative before launch, and report outcomes (conversion rate, sales cycle, forecast accuracy, attainment, renewal, and expansion) rather than activity.

- 
Build and run change plans: stakeholder mapping, communication cadence, interlock with enablement, adoption tracking, and feedback loops. Explain the why behind each change in the language of the audience, from reps and front-line managers to the CRO and ELT.

- 
Stay close to the field through deal reviews, pipeline inspection, and field sessions. Collect feedback continuously, adapt the approach quickly, and close the loop with the people who gave it.

- 
Align Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Enablement, Finance, and Systems on priorities, sequencing, and ownership, often without direct authority. Balance regional needs against global standards.

- 
Standardise global processes and operating cadence (forecast, pipeline inspection, QBRs) for scalability and repeatability.

- 
Provide narrative and analysis for QBRs, leadership meetings, and strategic discussions, linking initiative results to ARR, NRR, and GRR.

Experience & Qualifications 

The ideal candidate will:

- 
Bring 5+ years in sales operations, field operations, revenue operations, or a related function in B2B SaaS. We welcome current ICs, and managers willing to move into an IC role for the medium term (1+ years).

- 
Have a track record of delivering global initiatives with measurable business outcomes, and before and after metrics to show for it.

- 
Have led process, tooling, or organisational changes that the field adopted, with proven change management and communication skills at every level up to executive.

- 
Have field credibility: you have worked directly with Sales Leaders and sellers, and both trust you.

- 
Take feedback well and pivot quickly without losing sight of the outcome.

- 
Build strong relationships and influence across the GTM organisation without relying on direct authority.

- 
Combine business, strategy, and analytical capability, including forecasting, pipeline, and productivity analysis, and be able to articulate trends in churn, expansion, ARR, NRR, GRR, LTV, and CAC.

- 
Be hands-on with Salesforce, Google Sheets/Excel, and Tableau. AI power user.

- 
Operate with an owner mindset, and be comfortable diving deep and navigating ambiguity.

- 
Nice to have: experience in post-sales or Customer Success Operations (a plus, not a requirement); experience in a high-growth SaaS company, including a high-volume, PLG, or inbound-demand funnel; experience rolling out initiatives across regions in a multinational organisation.

In-office culture 

We're intentional about this. We believe the best teams are built in the room together. Three anchor days — Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays — create the collaboration rhythm that makes a hub office worth having. 

Candidates need to be genuinely based in the location the role is posted — if that's not where you are today, we're happy to support relocation for the right person.

We value diversity, equity, and inclusion

title: Partner Solutions Engineer
description:
Retire the ERP. 

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our AI-native financial platform gives modern, global companies automated accounting, real-time reporting and financial flows that move at the speed of the business. In a short time we've become the operating core for companies like Lovable, Legora and Keyshot.

The largest finance transformations don't start with a demo. They start with a Big 4 firm or a technology partner putting Light through its paces on behalf of their clients. Come help us win those rooms and make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

The role 

TLDR: Be the technical lead when Big 4 firms and technology partners evaluate Light, and turn those evaluations into strategic enterprise deals.

Before a Deloitte, PwC, EY or KPMG practice recommends Light to its clients, or a tech vendor builds Light into its offering, they test us hard: scripted scenarios, self-paced proof-of-value windows, architecture and security reviews, then a readout to their partners. You run that cycle end to end. You'll work directly with our founders, Partnerships, Sales and Product, and as an early member of the team you'll write the playbook every future partner evaluation follows.

What you'll do 

- Run partner evaluations end to end. Turn a partner's test scenarios into scripts, environments and success criteria; run self-paced proof-of-value windows with weekly check-ins; lead the final readout.

- Be the technical voice in the room. Run tailored demos and deep dives for Big 4 advisory and audit teams, CFO-office practices and vendor architects. Own objections on integrations, data migration, security, controls and audit trail.

- Map Light to complex finance. Translate multi-entity, multi-currency, consolidation, revenue recognition and statutory reporting requirements into how Light handles them, and say clearly where it doesn't yet.

- Enable partners to sell and deliver Light. Build demo environments, playbooks, reference architectures and certification content so partner teams can run Light without us in the room.

- Close strategic deals. Partner with Sales and Partnerships on joint account plans, enterprise scoping and solution design through to signature and handover to Implementation.

- Feed the roadmap. Bring patterns from every evaluation back to Product and Engineering, and build AI-powered tooling that makes the next evaluation faster.

What you'll bring 

- 4+ years as a Solutions Engineer, Solutions Consultant or Pre-Sales lead for ERP or finance software (vendor side preferred), or in a Big 4 ERP / finance transformation practice.

- A strong accounting foundation: close, consolidation, intercompany, multi-currency, revenue recognition and controls. You can hold your own with a Big 4 partner or a group controller.

- Hands-on experience with at least one major ERP (NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics or Workday) and real implementation projects: data migration, integrations, APIs.

- A track record of running structured evaluations, RFPs or proofs of concept with large or demanding buyers, and winning them.

- Executive presence and crisp writing. You make complex things simple, in a demo, a workshop or a one-page readout.

- Genuinely AI-native. You've changed how you work because of AI tooling, not just added it to your workflow.

Bonus points 

- Ex-Big 4 (advisory or audit) and a qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CPA or equivalent).

- Experience in a partner or alliances SE role, building channel enablement programs.

- Exposure to IFRS and local GAAP across several European markets, and SOC 2 / ISO 27001 security reviews.

- You've configured AI agents in production or built your own tools with them.

Probably not for you if: you've used ChatGPT once and weren't impressed, or you prefer a polished demo script to a hard question from an auditor.

title: Growth Marketing Manager
description:
Growth Marketing Manager 

Retire the ERP 

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers - automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Fuse Energy.

We're an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you're excited to modernise how companies run money, you're in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors including Balderton and Atomico and advised by industry titans, we're building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

Finance deserves better 

Finance teams at fast-growing companies run global, real-time businesses on a patchwork of legacy ERPs and point solutions. Every new entity, market or tool adds another system to stitch together and another hire to keep the numbers reconciled.

Light gives them a way out.

We build the finance solution that lets finance teams have it all, through three parts that work as one:

- Our ledger records every transaction across every entity in real time, so the numbers hold up from day one.

- Our apps adapt Light to how each business runs, from procurement to billing to reporting.

- Our agents operate the repetitive work that used to need another hire, so finance teams spend their time on the decisions that matter.

We take on the ERP and the legacy point solution world with something fast to implement, AI-native from the ground up, and better the more you use it.

Today we run the finance function for companies like Lovable, Legora and Keyshot, with backing from Atomico, Balderton, Seedcamp, Cherry and Entrée, and teams across Copenhagen, London and Stockholm, with remotes world over.

The Role 

We're looking for a Growth Marketing Manager to join our growth team and open up the channels we haven't really touched yet.

We've built a lean, efficient demand generation engine on the core paid channels you'd expect at a Series A B2B company, with Google Ads and LinkedIn doing the heavy lifting. It works, and it fills our pipeline every month. Now we want to find the next sources of pipeline, and we need someone who knows how to build them from scratch.

You'll work alongside our Senior Growth Marketing Manager, VP Marketing and the wider marketing team, with the freedom to test, learn and scale the channels that move the number. You'll sit close to sales, product and design, and you'll own the results of everything you launch.

We may hire more than one person through this process, so if you go deep on some of these channels rather than all of them, we still want to hear from you.

What You'll Be Doing 

- Building a referral programme that turns happy customers, partners and finance leaders into a steady source of pipeline.

- Running G2 and Capterra campaigns that put Light in front of buyers at the moment they compare options, and turning our reviews into proof across every channel.

- Launching and scaling Meta Ads for B2B, testing creative and audiences until you find what drives qualified pipeline.

- Finding the creators and influencers finance teams follow, writing briefs that land and scaling their content into campaigns that drive pipeline.

- Growing our presence across search and AI answer engines, so that when a finance leader asks Google or ChatGPT about ERP alternatives, Light shows up.

- Setting up measurement for each new channel with RevOps, so we know what every dollar returns.

- Sharing what you learn with the team, doubling down on what works and cutting what doesn't.

What We Think* You'll Need 

- Enough years in growth to know how to take a channel from zero to pipeline at a fast-growing B2B SaaS company.

- Hands-on experience across referrals, review sites, Meta Ads, influencer marketing or SEO and GEO. We don't expect you to master all five, so show us where you go deep.

- A test-and-learn mindset, with the discipline to measure every experiment against pipeline and revenue.

- Comfort with numbers and tools, from ad platforms to HubSpot to spreadsheets.

- An eye for creative and a feel for what makes finance people stop scrolling.

- Deep curiosity about how AI is reshaping marketing, finance and the companies we serve.

- A can-do, empathetic and collaborative spirit. No brilliant assholes here, please.

*If the core of the role sounds compelling but you don't tick every box, we'd still love for you to reach out and convince us you're the right person.

The Good Stuff 

- A five-day, in-office culture with a high-density team in Copenhagen.

- A competitive salary and potential stock options.

- 25 days of annual leave plus public holidays in the country where you're based.

- Regular socials and two company offsites a year.

- The chance to build new growth channels from the ground up at a company defining a new category.

title: Data Engineering Lead
description:
About Plasma

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.

At first you'll build much of the platform yourself: our Snowflake warehouse, the pipelines that feed it and the modelled layer on top. As the function grows, you'll choose the tools, set the standards and hire the team.

The Work 

- Own Plasma's data platform end to end: the Snowflake warehouse, ingestion from production systems and third-party providers, and the modelled layer the rest of the company builds on

- Define the metrics the company runs on, including funded users, activation, engagement, balances, spend and retention, and make sure every team uses the same definitions

- Design and analyse experiments, and be clear about when a result is real and when it isn't

- Work with Payments and finance so the business can trust its numbers: reconciliation across ledgers, providers and banking partners, revenue reporting and unit economics

- Find fraudulent and abusive patterns across onboarding, funding, card spend and transfers, and build the signals and rules that let risk and operations act on them

- Treat data quality, testing, access control and PII handling as part of the platform, not an afterthought

- Choose tools deliberately, set standards for the function and hire the team as Plasma scales

The Bar 

- A senior, hands-on data practitioner with a track record of both building a data platform and using it

- Deep SQL and data modelling skills, with enough engineering range to build and run production pipelines yourself

- Comfortable starting from very little, and building something that still makes sense when the team is five times bigger

- Strong judgment on tradeoffs: speed vs. rigour, build vs. buy, a quick answer now vs. a reusable model later

- You communicate clearly, write clean, tested code, and lead through technical decisions whether or not you're managing people yet

- You have very high agency. You don't wait to be told which problem to work on; you go and find the ones that matter

Nice to have

- Hands-on fraud, risk or financial-crime analytics

- Familiarity with stablecoins and on-chain data, including how blockchain transactions map to accounts, balances and ledgers

- Experience hiring and growing a data team

- Machine learning in production for fraud, risk or personalisation

- Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

title: Staff Engineer, EU Infrastructure
description:
About Wolt 

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life. 

About the Team

Our Infrastructure teams build the foundation that engineers at Wolt, Deliveroo, and DoorDash build on: the compute, cloud, and networking capabilities that enable Engineering teams to develop, deploy, and run services at global scale. The EU Compute team has a specific focus on provisioning, scaling, and the efficient operation of GPU infrastructure for AI and ML workloads. This is an emerging space with plenty of greenfield opportunities.

We're looking for a Staff Engineer to be a hands-on technical leader for this infrastructure work that crosses team and brand boundaries. You'll set direction for the platform, turn complex problems into deliverable plans, write and review production code, and help other engineers make sound decisions. It's an exciting time to join: we're building a global platform and the choices made now will shape how engineers across the company ship for years.

What you’ll be doing

You'll own some of the hardest infrastructure problems in the company and make the platform easier to operate and safer to build on. We’re determined to build great platform products and user experiences, and you’ll be pivotal in making this reality.

Day-to-day in this role you’ll:

- Set technical direction for shared AWS and Kubernetes infrastructure, balancing reliability, security, developer experience, and cost.

- Lead substantial initiatives from design through rollout and operation, coordinating dependencies and decisions across Wolt, Deliveroo and DoorDash, focusing on workloads targeting GPUs.

- Evolve Kubernetes clusters, cloud networking, identity, and infrastructure provisioning to support growing and varied workloads.

- Build reusable Terraform patterns and self-service tooling that help teams provision infrastructure safely and consistently.

- Improve deployment and operational practices, including GitOps, observability, capacity planning, incident response and recovery.

- Use production signals and developer feedback to find platform friction, choose where to invest and measure whether changes actually help.

- Assist with supporting the platform, with deep focus on GPU infrastructure, as well as broad focus on compute in general.

- Gracefully sunset legacy infrastructure and tooling, and create strategies to reduce toil.

- Mentor engineers through design reviews, implementation and incidents, raising the quality of infrastructure work across teams.

Our humble expectations

- Deep experience building and operating Kubernetes and AWS infrastructure in production. Familiarity with GPU workloads and orchestration is a plus.

- Strong software engineering skills: you use Go, Python or a similar language to build maintainable tools and automation.

- Experience with infrastructure as code (we use Terraform) and with designing systems that other engineering teams depend on.

- A track record of leading complex technical work across teams, including architectural decisions, delivery, and operational follow-through. You have the breadth to collaborate and design across team and domain boundaries, and the depth to have hands-on impact.

- Strong judgment on trade-offs in distributed systems, networking, security, reliability, and cloud cost.

- Clear communication, and the ability to bring people together around a practical technical direction.

What we offer

- Scope and influence. Shape infrastructure used globally, while staying close to the engineering. Your work will help product teams ship services with greater ease and confidence.

- Real problems at global scale. Multi-cluster Kubernetes, AI / ML workloads, cloud networking, GitOps, and progressive delivery across a global company.

- Autonomy and ownership. Set direction and see it through from design to operation, with the backing of a global engineering organisation spanning Europe and the US.

- Great people. Work with talented engineers and leaders in a diverse, international environment, mentoring and learning from others.

We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. title: Staff Technical Programme Manager, Systems Software
description:
About IonQ: 

IonQ, Inc . [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance .

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. 

Role: 

System Software builds the software that runs IonQ's quantum computers: the runtime, orchestration, quantum tools, controllers and transport software that sit between the Quantum Operating System and the hardware. It is where a next-generation system either comes together or doesn't.

We're hiring a Staff Technical Programme Manager to lead delivery across this stack. You'll report to the Group Program Manager, Software in our Programme Management Office and be matrixed to the VP, Software for day-to-day work.

You'll work across five engineering teams (runtime, orchestration, quantum tools, controllers and transport) and the interfaces between them and their cross-functional stakeholders, serving several next-generation system programmes at once, with hardware being co-developed alongside the software and teams in both Oxford and the US. Those programmes draw on the same engineers, so the central problem of this role is making sure that capacity is spent by decision, not by default.

We run a centralised PMO model. This role will not own engineering headcount or define product but it will make the programme around those things run. It carries real ownership of delivery: the plan, the trade-offs put in front of decision-makers, and the honesty of the status. In this role you will interface with everyone from technical software engineers to a wide range of the most senior stakeholders. You will also coordinate with your fellow programme managers, across Science, Infrastructure and broader Software teams, making sure all plans are shared and coordinated, rather than operating in silos.

Turning a research-grade quantum system into a dependable product is a problem nobody has finished solving, and the delivery standard you'll work within is being built now. If writing the first version of the plan sounds like the interesting part, we should talk.

Responsibilities: 

In this role you will own the end-to-end delivery of the Systems Software roadmap across several concurrent programmes including managing dependencies between hardware, science and systems integration teams. You will partner closely with engineering leadership, the engineering teams run the day to day planning and boards, you will provide the direction that creates incremental milestones that ship.

You will identify risks and blockers early and work with the teams to resolve them. You will also run intake and triage, so requests reach the right team with the right priority and engineers can stay focused on planned work.

Key responsibilities include:

- 
Make contention visible: when two programmes need the same team in the same quarter, bring it to the right decision-maker with the options and a recommendation before it becomes a slip.

- 
Keep the systems of record honest. Requirements, plans, schedules and Jira drift apart; you'll close the gap and automate the checking.

- 
Make invisible work visible: on-call load, sustaining work and technical debt tracked as rigorously as feature delivery.

- 
Surface risks early, before you have a full solution or complete alignment. We'd rather hear it messy and on time.

- 
Run intake and triage so requests reach the right team, with priority set by the people who own it, and engineers stay on planned work.

- 
Work hand in hand with the Quantum Systems Infrastructure and Science TPMs in Oxford and the Software TPMs in the US: shared processes where teams meet, and no duplicated ceremonies, boards or reports.

- 
Write concise, plain-English status on progress, risks and decisions for programme directors, engineering leaders and senior leadership.

- 
Help shape how IonQ runs software delivery across sites, working with the Group Program Manager, Software on the shared delivery standard.

Requirements: 

You will have significant experience running technical programmes across several software teams, ideally in systems, embedded, compiler or platform software. You can discuss scope and trade-offs directly with engineering leads, read and reason about code, and re-plan when a timeline is no longer realistic. You will have a track record of leading teams through genuine ambiguity, writing the first version of the plan when there isn't one, not just executing a defined one.

You can break broad problems down into specific, assignable actions, and you have designed a team's operating cadence before. No quantum background is needed. Experience of software that works closely with hardware, for example in labs, robotics, aerospace or scientific instruments, would be beneficial.

You’d be a great fit with:

- 
A habit of turning diffuse problems into specific, minimal, assignable asks.

- 
Technical fluency to engage engineering leads directly on scope and trade-offs, and comfort reading and reasoning about code.

- 
Willingness to re-baseline against reality rather than defend dates that have stopped being true, and the judgement to tell a target that motivates from one that just generates fiction.

- 
Experience with software that works closely with hardware: labs, robotics, aerospace, scientific instruments or similar.

- 
A chase-without-nagging, escalate-without-drama style, and a clear sense of the difference between a risk and a noise.

- 
AI as a core part of how you work, for example agent-driven tracking, reconciliation or reporting.

- 
Clear, concise written and verbal communication with both technical and senior stakeholders.

Additional desirable skills include capacity and staffing modelling, designing operating cadences and experience leading work across sites and time zones. Experience working with programmes and systems such as Jira, Confluence and GitHub, with a preference for lightweight processes, is also helpful.

Job ID: 1948

The Role: 

We are looking for a Senior Receiving Inspector to join our Quality team. As a Senior Receiving Inspector, you’ll be part of a cross-functional team whose mission is to lead IonQ on its journey to build the world’s best quantum computers to solve the world’s most complex problems. 

You will make sure that incoming, in-process and finished components meet their mechanical, electrical and PCBA specifications. You will also own the inspection side of the Material Review Board process, from handling and containing nonconforming material, through the inspection actions the board assigns, to verifying, closing and tracking nonconformance records once the Quality Engineer has given the disposition. As the senior technical resource for inspection, you will allocate the daily inspection work and guide less experienced inspectors. The ideal candidate combines technical expertise with the integrity to hold quality standards under production pressure.

Responsibilities :

Day to day, you will inspect incoming parts, in-process production and finished goods against approved specifications, drawings and purchase order requirements, deciding the inspection method and sequence with little instruction. You will interpret drawing callouts and datum structures to GD&T and ASME Y14.5, turn them into inspection plans and acceptance criteria, apply statistical sampling plans and use the right metrology instruments, including programming and running CMM, OMM or vision systems. You will support the calibration schedule, remove out of tolerance equipment from service and keep the inspection area to the local 5S procedure.

When something is wrong, you will control it. You will identify, tag, segregate and quarantine nonconforming material with correct lot and serial traceability to ISO 9001 and AS9100, sweep stock and work in progress to contain every affected lot, write the nonconformance record and present the inspection evidence at the Material Review Board. You will carry out the actions the board assigns, verify scrap disposal so nothing returns to the supply chain, and feed inspection data to the Quality Engineer for root cause analysis and supplier corrective action. You will also support internal, customer and regulatory audits, and keep to the quality management system, export control and customer contract requirements for controlled material and data.

Key responsibilities include: 

- Leading daily inspection of incoming, in-process and finished goods, including allocating the workload and verifying other inspectors' results and records before release

- Writing nonconformance records, presenting inspection evidence at the Material Review Board and completing assigned actions such as screening, sorting and rework verification

- Verifying and closing nonconformance records against the Quality Engineer's disposition, and keeping the MRB log and ageing report up to date

- Drafting and releasing inspection procedures and work instructions, and reporting metrics such as first pass yield, defect Pareto, NCR ageing and inspection turnaround

- Working with engineering, manufacturing, supply chain and suppliers on source inspection, first article inspection and quality problems

Requirements: 

You will bring six or more years of related experience in a regulated manufacturing environment, including proven PCBA inspection to IPC-A-610 and experience of aerospace inspection processes and standards. You will have hands-on experience of controlling nonconforming product and of the Material Review Board process, and of using a Quality Management System or ERP nonconformance module to raise, track and close records and actions.

You read and interpret complex technical drawings with a thorough understanding of datum structures to ASME Y14.5, and you are expert with layout tools such as surface plates, height gauges, indicators, callipers, micrometers, gauge blocks and thread gauges. You have allocated work to, trained and guided less experienced inspectors, and you are confident with standard office software for data analysis and documentation. The role involves lifting up to 18 kg and standing for long periods, with strict adherence to safety and PPE requirements.

You’d be a great fit with:

- Clear communication at every level, from management to engineers and physicists, when resolving complex quality issues

- Working knowledge of root cause analysis methods such as 5 Why, Ishikawa or 8D

- Experience of first article inspection to AS9102 and of source inspection at supplier sites

- An ASQ Certified Quality Inspector or Certified Quality Technician qualification, or equivalent

- A quality first, self-starting approach, with precision under pressure and a willingness to support other quality functions

title: Manager: Compliance Advisory (and Data Protection)
location: London or remote within the UK
description:
About Griffin 

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do 

Our culture 

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture. 

The Team 

You'll join our Service guild and work across first line operations, sales and produt. Working closely with Protect (our second line) you'll be the first person dedicated to compliance within the team. You'll define what great compliance solutions look like. Then implement them , keeping Griffin's products and customer outcomes in shape as we grow.

The opportunity 

We want compliance and data protection built into how we design, sell and run our products, not bolted at the end.

As our hands on compliance adviser in the first line (the teams who run the business and own its risks), you'll bring regulatory expertise to help our operations, commercial and product teams do exactly that. With card issuing and other launches coming up, there's plenty to get stuck into.

Compliance advisory is the heart of this role and will take around 70% of your time. You’ll also pick up a smaller, complementary slice of work as our Data Protection Officer (DPO), around 30% of your time. DPO experience is a plus but not essential, and we’ll train you if you need it.

What success looks like 

In your first year, compliance advisory is where you’ve made your mark. You’ve sought out our operations, sales and product teams and shown them that working with you makes things smoother, not slower. Now they bring you in early by default. You’ve guided at least one major launch, like card issuing, from first idea to go live. You’ve put clear governance and outcome monitoring in place for our live products, so Protect (our second line risk and compliance team) sees fewer surprises and finds a stronger compliance foundation.

Alongside that, in the smaller DPO part of your role, you’ve taken ownership of our data protection agenda. You’ve gone looking for ways to improve, made the changes happen, and given our senior leaders an honest picture of where we stand.

To do this you'll be involved in: 

Compliance advisory (around 70% of your time) 

- Product development: turning regulation into clear requirements, customer journeys, T&Cs and fair value assessments, from first idea through product approval to launch, with data protection built in from the start.

- Product lifecycle management: keeping live products compliant through periodic fair value assessments, outcome monitoring, reviews, changes and closures.

- Sales: helping our commercial team check early whether potential partners fit our risk appetite, and reviewing sales material.

- Marketing: working on marketing materials, both ours and our customers’, to make sure they comply with regulation and our own policies, and that our financial promotions are properly challenged.

- Service (Operations): building regulatory and data protection requirements into how Service works day to day, with procedures and controls people actually use.

- Regulatory change: working out what new rules mean for us, and making sure the right teams make the right changes on time.

- Issues and reporting: investigating and fixing compliance issues, including personal data breaches, and reporting clearly on compliance risks and customer outcomes.

- Working with second line (Protect): bringing them in early, sharing the evidence they need, and acting on their challenge.

Data Protection Officer (around 30% of your time - training will be provided if needed) 

Being our DPO means:

- advising our teams on their obligations, including data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) and transfer risk assessments (TRAs)

- monitoring how well we comply with the UK GDPR, other global data protection laws and our own policies

- training colleagues and raising awareness of data protection

- being our contact point for the ICO and for people with questions or requests about their data

As our DPO, you’ll report directly to our COO and have the independence you need to do the job well. We’ll involve you early in anything that affects personal data.

We expect you to shape this role: This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background 

We need a proactive compliance doer first and foremost. You get stuck in without waiting to be asked, and you’re comfortable tackling regulations you haven’t met before. You use your experience and expertise to help our teams find simple, clear and compliant solutions. Your advice is balanced, easy to follow and focused on the risks that matter most. You want to push the business forward, and you see good compliance as part of how we get there.

To ensure this, we're looking for people who have:

- Compliance experience in the first (preferred) or second line of a UK regulated firm, ideally a bank, e-money institution or payments firm.

- Practical knowledge of the rules behind our products , like Consumer Duty, BCOBS, CASS, FISMA, the Payment Services Regulations and the Money Laundering Regulations. As well as familiarity with HMRC requirements like BBSI and AEOI reporting.

- Hands-on experience turning regulation into practical requirements for product, sales or operations teams.

- An openness to picking up data protection as part of the role: a genuine interest is enough, DPO experience isn’t required.

- A curious, questioning approach. You know the right questions to ask before signing something off, not just the rules to check it against.

- The confidence to challenge, clearly and kindly, when something isn’t right.

- A love of writing . We have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write ).

Ideally, you would also:

- Have deep expertise in at least one specialist area, such as payments, cards, Consumer Duty, BCOBS, financial promotions or similar.

- Have been a DPO, or worked closely with one, in a regulated firm.

- Have worked in finance or banking. 

What can we offer you? 

We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future.

- Salary: £ 80-90 (DOE)

- Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK

- Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

- Time off: 25 days’ holiday, bank holidays and a winter break (we shut down between Christmas and New Year)

- Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

- Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

- Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

- Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

- Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

- AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

- Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks 

How long will the process take? 

We move as fast as possible, but it normally takes us about 2-3 weeks to get to know to each other.

- Step 1: An initial phone call with our Talent Team for us to tell you more about Griffin and learn about your recent experience.

- Step 2: Meet your manager to talk through your experience and how that relates to the requirements.

- Step 3: A task based on what you’ll be doing on a day to day at Griffin.

- Step 4: Meet with peers in your team for a more in-depth technical interview.

- Step 5 : Culture and Founder interview: Learn more about this here .

How do I apply? 

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We’re remote-first 

We trust people to do great work wherever they are. We hire across the UK and most of our team works remotely full-time. We have a small London office in Moorgate for those who want it, and about a third of the company is close enough to use it occasionally, but there's no expectation to be there. What matters is the work, not where you do it.

Under representation 

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

We are looking for a builder: someone who would rather create a market than inherit one. Our first enterprise customers are live and the signal is clear. Everything after that is yours to build.

Putting physical AI onto a production line is not a software sale. It reaches the plant manager, the COO, the unions, health and safety, IT, procurement, and often the CEO. Nice to Have

- You have run pilots, POCs, or hardware-plus-software deals.

- You have been early somewhere: founding AE, first sales hire, or early Head of Sales.

- A background in operations consulting, VC, or as a founder.

Who Will Thrive at microagi

Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits:

- Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it.

- Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it.

- Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them.

- Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes.

Leveraging strong fundamentals in thermal physics and cooling strategies, you will guide analyses of complex thermal management systems, fluid flow dynamics, and heat dissipation challenges, including both steady-state and transient thermal behavior. Your team will help customers evaluate critical factors such as thermal risk, component reliability, power density, and cooling efficiency to architect cutting-edge thermal management systems for next-generation hardware.

You will work closely with customer engineering teams to understand their technical challenges, provide expert guidance, and clearly articulate Vinci's capabilities in solving real-world problems. You will also serve as a key feedback channel to product and engineering teams, translating customer insights into actionable inputs that shape product direction and drive continuous improvement.

This is a remote role, with close collaboration with Sales, Product, and Engineering in Palo Alto, CA, USA. The role includes moderate travel, primarily within continental Europe. Some infrequent intercontinental travel may be required for discussions and collaboration with the US team.

Responsibilities

Qualifications (Minimum Qualifications) 

- Education: Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related technical field.

- Technical depth: Expert-level mastery of commercial simulation software (Flotherm, Ansys Icepak/Fluent, Simcenter STAR-CCM+, or equivalent), with 15+ years of hands-on experience in thermal management and cooling solutions, either as a practitioner running simulations or as a technical account manager for commercial physics simulation software.

- Industry domain: Deep familiarity with semiconductor electronics packaging, advanced packaging technologies (e.g., 2.5D/3D IC), or foundry ecosystems.

- Customer engagement: Prior experience in dedicated customer-facing roles, with a strong ability to build trust and manage engineering client relationships.

- Automation & scripting: Practical programming experience using Python or C++ to automate workflows or parse simulation data.

- Leadership impact: Proven track record of prior managerial or technical leadership experience, with the ability to scale, mentor, and drive execution across engineering teams.

- Communication: Elite interpersonal and communication skills, with a proven ability to distill complex physics and simulation results into clear, high-impact narratives for both deep technical panels and business-oriented executives.

Preferred (Desirable Differentiators) 

- Multiphysics breadth: Familiarity with structural mechanical simulations (FEA/stress) and/or Electrical Signal Integrity and Power Integrity (SI/PI) workflows.

- Commercial track record: Direct experience commercializing technical software, ideally electronic design automation (EDA) or CAE simulation tools, into major semiconductor and electronics enterprises.

- Go-to-market experience: Prior experience within technical pre-sales, application engineering (FAE), or strategic technical sales environments.

- Emerging tech adjacency: Ability to rapidly adopt and champion next-generation, physics-based workflows and AI-assisted design or simulation tools.

Why Join Us 

- Don't just use AI; help redefine how next-generation hardware is designed.

- Work at the convergence of state-of-the-art AI models, fundamental physics, and high-stakes enterprise engineering.

- Collaborate with world-class engineers and researchers in a fast-moving startup environment.

À propos de Vinci 

Vinci développe une IA fondée sur la physique (Physics AI) pour la conception de systèmes hardware. Notre plateforme donne aux équipes de conception et de simulation des prédictions physiques précises, obtenues en une fraction du temps d'une simulation classique, et qui s'intègrent à leurs outils existants.

C'est la première solution à offrir à la fois la rigueur de la simulation traditionnelle et la vitesse de l'IA. Elle transforme la façon dont les semi-conducteurs les plus avancés au monde sont conçus, vérifiés et mis en production.

About Anthropic 

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role 

As an Enterprise Account Executive at Anthropic, you'll join the foundational team at the forefront of introducing our cutting-edge AI productivity API and SaaS solutions to retail organisations across France. You'll drive the adoption of safe, frontier AI by securing strategic deals with retail, grocery, fashion, and e-commerce companies. You'll leverage your consultative sales expertise in the retail sector to propel revenue growth while becoming a trusted partner to retail stakeholders, helping them embed and deploy AI while uncovering its full range of capabilities in merchandising and supply chain, store operations, e-commerce and marketing, and customer service. In collaboration with GTM, Product, and Marketing teams, you'll continuously refine our value proposition, sales methodology, and market positioning to resonate with retail decision-makers.

The ideal candidate will have a passion for developing new market segments, pinpointing high-potential opportunities, and executing strategies to capture them. By driving deployment of Anthropic's emerging products, you will help enterprises obtain new capabilities while also advancing the ethical development of AI.

- Demonstrated ability to navigate retail organisational structures and procurement processes, building consensus among diverse stakeholders including executives, business and operations leadership, and IT departments

- Fluent in French and English

- A passion for and/or experience with advanced AI systems and their applications. You feel strongly about ensuring frontier AI systems are developed safely and ethically for retail use

En tant qu'Enterprise Account Executive chez Anthropic, vous rejoindrez l'équipe fondatrice chargée de faire découvrir notre API de productivité IA de pointe et nos solutions SaaS aux entreprises du secteur de la distribution et du commerce en France. - Une solide expérience de la gestion de cycles de vente complexes au sein d'entreprises du retail et de la conclusion de contrats stratégiques, fondée sur une compréhension fine des exigences techniques comme des cas d'usage du secteur

- D'excellentes compétences en communication et l'aisance nécessaire pour présenter devant des publics variés du retail, des équipes opérationnelles et digitales jusqu'aux membres de la direction

- Une connaissance approfondie des cycles d'achat, des processus de décision et des principales problématiques du secteur du retail

- Une approche stratégique et analytique du marché du retail, alliée à une exécution tactique et créative pour saisir les opportunités

- Un intérêt marqué pour les systèmes d'IA avancés et leurs applications, voire une expérience dans ce domaine. Le développement sûr et éthique des systèmes d'IA de pointe pour les usages du retail vous tient particulièrement à cœur.
