We are looking for an experienced Senior Manager to serve as an AI Architect — someone who can design the end-to-end architecture for enterprise AI platforms, lead consultancy engagements, and grow our AI & Solutions Engineering capability. 

The AI Architect role owns the technical blueprint for AI-enabled solutions delivered in and around our clients’ environments, combining deep architectural specialism with the commercial and leadership skills to shape and grow our practice. This is a role for someone who thrives at the intersection of client advisory, AI platform architecture and hands-on delivery leadership — and who has a genuine passion for bringing AI systems to production at scale. 

What you will be doing 

As a Senior Manager and AI Architect, you will own and lead the architecture of complex AI programmes end-to-end — from shaping the opportunity and winning the work, through solution design, delivery governance and team leadership. You will bring SME-level depth in enterprise AI architecture and apply it to create real, lasting value for our clients. 

Although we do not expect you to be an expert in every technology listed below simultaneously, our team consists of people who can advise clients as well as bring deep technical knowledge when needed. Key responsibilities span the following areas. 

Engagement & delivery leadership 

- Own and lead the architecture of complex AI and data transformation engagements, taking accountability for solution design, quality, technical risk and client outcomes. 

- Lead and resource multi-disciplinary delivery teams — architects, engineers, data scientists and consultants — providing clear direction, technical oversight and people development. 

- Manage engagement resourcing: forecast team requirements, work with practice leadership to staff engagements, and develop the talent pipeline through mentoring of junior practitioners. 

- Proactively identify and manage delivery and architectural risks in complex stakeholder environments, escalating appropriately and maintaining client confidence throughout. 

- Communicate clearly to both technical teams and senior client stakeholders, translating architectural complexity into actionable insight and decisive recommendation. 

- Conduct rigorous architecture and design reviews and uphold engineering standards across every engagement you lead. 

Stakeholder management & advisory 

- Act as a trusted advisor to client architects, CTOs, CDAOs and engineering leads, earning trust through depth of knowledge and a demonstrable delivery track record. 

- Build and maintain strong, senior client relationships, navigating competing priorities across business, technology and risk functions. 

- Facilitate architecture workshops and decision forums, driving alignment across diverse stakeholder groups and securing buy-in for target-state designs. 

- Translate business strategy into architectural roadmaps, sequencing investment and change in a way that balances ambition with deliverability. 

Business development & bid support 

- Play a leading role in business development: identifying new opportunities, shaping propositions, and supporting or leading bids and tender responses for AI and technology engagements. 

- Contribute to proposal writing, articulating our capabilities and differentiators, including authoring technical and architecture sections of bid responses to client tenders and RFPs. 

- Support practice-level growth initiatives, including account planning, capability development, and go-to-market positioning for AI architecture and solutions engineering services. 

Technical architecture — what you will design 

You will be the design authority for enterprise AI platforms, able to reason across the full stack and make credible technology selections. We expect expert-level depth in several of the areas below and working knowledge across the rest. 

AI platform & cloud architecture 

- Architect AI and Data Platforms using a mix of technologies including Databricks, Snowflake, Claude Enterprise and the native services of Azure, AWS and GCP - selecting the right tool for the workload rather than defaulting to a single vendor. 

- Design for scalability, security, cost efficiency and multi-cloud / hybrid patterns, with a strong grasp of containerisation, infrastructure-as-code, event-driven architectures and CI/CD. 

- Balance technical excellence with delivery pragmatism and commercial realities, championing the path from prototype to production. 

Enterprise AI ecosystem integration 

- Bring awareness of the broader enterprise landscape and how AI integrates with core operational systems such as SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow and other systems of record and engagement. 

- Design integration patterns that let AI capabilities interoperate safely with enterprise data, identity, workflow and process automation platforms – including MCP and A2A and how these capabilities enable an enterprise Agent mesh. 

- Understand the data, governance and change implications of embedding AI into mission-critical enterprise processes. 

Orchestration & control plane 

- Architect the orchestration and control-plane layer that governs how AI capabilities are exposed, routed and managed across the enterprise. 

- Design MCP, AI and LLM gateway layers for secure, observable and policy-controlled access to models and tools. 

- Design agent and skills registries — including recommending suitable technologies and patterns — to enable discovery, reuse and governance of agentic capabilities. 

- Define the control plane for routing, rate limiting, cost management, model selection and version control across multiple model providers. 

AI solution design 

- Design retrieval and reasoning architectures including RAG, corrective RAG (CRAG), and agentic patterns, selecting the right approach for a given business problem. 

- Architect agent harnesses and their components — planning, memory, tool use, state management and multi-agent coordination. 

- Design prompt strategies, context management and grounding approaches for reliable, production-grade LLM behaviour. 

Evaluation, guardrails & responsible AI 

- Design evaluation frameworks and guardrails that make AI systems safe, reliable and measurable — covering accuracy, safety, bias, and task success. 

- Embed responsible-AI and governance controls aligned to emerging regulation and client risk appetites. 

- Define human-in-the-loop and fallback strategies for high-stakes use cases. 

Observability & operations 

- Architect logging, monitoring, tracing and cost-observability across the AI stack, including model, agent and platform telemetry. 

- Design for drift detection, performance monitoring and continuous evaluation in production (LLMOps / MLOps). 

- Establish operational patterns for reliability, incident response and lifecycle management of AI systems at scale. 

Your skills and experience 

We're seeking a technically credible, commercially aware leader who brings a rare combination of architectural depth, delivery accountability and client advisory skill — someone energised by the complexity of taking AI solutions to production at scale.

- Proven ability to architect enterprise AI platforms across a mix of technologies (Databricks, Snowflake, Azure, AWS, GCP) with strong design capability across cloud, data and AI domains. 

- Working understanding of how AI integrates with major operational systems such as SAP, Salesforce and ServiceNow. 

- Hands-on knowledge of agentic AI, LLM gateways, MCP, RAG/CRAG, agent harnesses, evaluations and guardrails, and AI observability. 

- Demonstrable experience designing and leading data & AI transformation programmes, and building high-performing teams in complex stakeholder environments — engaging comfortably at CTO, CDAO or engineering-director level. 

- Track record of supporting or leading bid and proposal activity, including writing technical and architecture sections of responses to tenders and RFPs.

- Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Data Science or a related discipline, or equivalent depth through relevant certifications (e.g. AWS Solutions Architect Professional, Google Professional ML Engineer, Databricks / Azure / GCP architecture credentials). 

Industry experience 

We would particularly like to hear from people who have designed and led data & AI transformation programmes across one or more of the following sectors:

title: AI Ops Engineer (Business Operations)
description:
About Kernel

Agents are starting to sell, buy and operate on behalf of companies. But before an agent can close a deal, qualify an account, route a lead or assess risk, it has to answer a basic question: which company is this?

Today, that answer is messy, and no one answers it reliably. Business identity lives across CRMs, ERPs and third-party datasets full of duplicates, missing parent companies, stale addresses and incorrect enrichment. The cost shows up across the enterprise: sales teams miss revenue opportunities because they lack the right account context; operations teams take on avoidable exposure because risk signals are fragmented or wrong; and finance teams end up chasing, writing off, or defaulting on bad debt that should have been caught earlier.

Humans have worked around that mess for years. Agents cannot. They need a reliable business identity layer they can trust.

Kernel is building that layer: the business registry for agents. We issue a permanent Kernel ID for every business, plus the context an agent needs to act on it. Ops, data and revenue teams at Gong, Legora, Mistral, Canva and Notion already use Kernel on their own systems. Agents are next, and there will be far more of them.

We have raised $20M from top VCs and operators at Plaid, OpenAI, Slack and others, and we are growing 10x YoY.

The Role

We’re looking for an AI Ops Engineer to build the internal systems that help Kernel scale without adding unnecessary manual work. You’ll work across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations - finding the highest-leverage problems and building practical AI-powered workflows.

This is a hands-on builder role. You’ll take ideas from a vague business problem to a tool or workflow that people use, then maintain and improve it in production. You’ll choose the fastest sensible approach for each problem - coding agents, automation platforms, APIs, data pipelines or lightweight code.

You’ll report to Arvin Ashrafi, Head of Finance & Operations , and partner closely with GTM, Marketing, and Customer Success leadership.

What You’ll Be Doing

- Define how an AI-native company operates: help build Kernel’s internal playbook for using AI across GTM, Marketing, Customer Success and Operations

- Build internal tools and workflows: use coding agents, APIs, automation platforms, no-code tools or lightweight code

- Turn company data into operational leverage: connect and improve data across our systems, then put it to work in AI agents, proactive workflows and better decision-making

- Put AI agents to work across Kernel: give teams agents with the right context, tools and guardrails so they can move faster without sacrificing judgement or reliability

- Be Kernel’s own internal customer: deploy Kernel on Kernel’s CRM, improve our GTM data and turn what you learn into useful feedback for Product and Engineering

- Level up the team: help colleagues become confident AI users, document what works and turn successful experiments into repeatable ways of working

Your First 6 Months

For your first six months, you’ll focus on our sales team. You’ll sit with our BDRs, AEs and Account Managers and learn how they work day to day. Then you’ll automate everything that doesn’t need a human. That means going deep on Salesforce and our GTM stack, and owning the RevOps workflows behind them. After that, you’ll bring the same approach to Marketing, Customer Success and Operations.

What You Bring

- A track record of shipping: you’ve built tools, automations or AI workflows that people use every day, ideally inside a small, fast-moving startup. Around 2–5 years of experience is typical, but what you’ve built matters more than your years. Ex-founders welcome

- Experience inside a high-growth startup, or building your own, is highly desirable

- Curious about sales: you’re keen to learn how our BDRs and AEs work, and how Salesforce is set up, before you build for them

- AI-tool obsessed: you are constantly testing new models, agents, MCPs and workflows, and you have the judgement to turn them into reliable systems that people actually adopt

- Strong data instincts: you can turn fragmented, messy information into reliable workflows and create feedback loops that keep it trustworthy

- Can’t unsee inefficiency: you see the company as a connected system; when you find a broken or unnecessarily manual process, your instinct is to understand it, build the fix and make sure it sticks

⚠️ This role may not be for you if you:

- Prefer deep specialization over breadth: this role means switching between projects and teams, depending on business needs

- Prefer steady-state work over project-based sprints: priorities will shift as the business evolves

- Only want “strategic” work: you will personally build the tools, clean the data and fix the workflows

❌ This role is definitely not for you if you:

- Need every task to be clearly scoped before starting: ambiguity and learning on the fly are constant

- Avoid operational grunt work or lose interest after the prototype

title: Staff Engineer - Platform & Tooling
description:
Who is Atominvest 

Atominvest is the operating system for modern private markets asset managers. Our modular, flexible SaaS technology underpins key investor- and portfolio-management workflows.

Our customers are sophisticated private equity, growth equity, and private credit firms managing billions in assets globally. We aim to deliver ongoing high-quality outcomes for them through a long-term partnership mindset.

At Atominvest, you’ll be working on something very exciting: the future of work, investments and sustainability/ ethical investing for the world’s best investors and delivering a positive impact through this. Based on the growth we are experiencing, we think we’re on to something big.

It won’t be easy. Joining a scale up business is an amazing and rewarding challenge, pushing well beyond the boundaries of natural growth cycles. You’ll move quicker than feels comfortable and be brilliant at continually re-prioritizing what must get done to keep Atominvest growing year over year at the pace of the best SaaS companies on the planet.

We’ve gone from zero to ten, now we’re looking to go from ten to one hundred!

About the role

Hi, I'm Thomas, VP Engineering at Atominvest. This is the hire I'm most excited about, so I wanted to tell you about it myself.

You'll own the platform our clients run on and build the AI development harness our engineers work in day to day. That work runs from infrastructure to application code, so we're looking for an experienced engineer with breadth across both, and depth in at least one. Together, it's what lets a small, lean team, working alongside AI agents, ship like a much bigger one.

By platform, we mean everything our product and our engineers stand on: infrastructure, security, test automation, developer experience, and the agent pipelines that run through all of them. It's a broad, hands-on role. You'll write infrastructure as code for a new service one day and address network vulnerabilities the next, then enhance our AI development harness and release a new feature, all within the same month.

You might be a platform engineer who loves shipping product, or a full-stack engineer who has run serious production infrastructure. Either works.

As deployments grow more complex, the team needs your depth in infrastructure and distributed systems. You'll strengthen the architecture and make the design decisions the platform will rest on for years. Those decisions should leave room to grow, because future products may bring much larger volumes of data than we handle today.

It has to stay dependable while we do it. Our software needs to be available around the clock, every day of the year, and data integrity is critical. Our clients use Atominvest to report to their own investors, so a wrong number matters as much as an outage. Security, reliability and audit-readiness matter too. If you enjoy getting those right without slowing everything else down, you'll find plenty of fun things to work on.

The machine that builds the product

We're becoming AI-native. Agents do more and more of the mechanical work of writing code, and engineers build the machine that builds the product: the architecture, the specs, the limits agents work within, and the evals that tell us whether their output is right.

I think that moves an engineer's leverage upstream. When code is cheap, the scarce things are judgement and understanding. Which problem is worth solving? What does good look like for the person using it? Is the output actually right? Did what we shipped help? The best engineers I've worked with always solved the end problem, with code as the medium. Now that's most of the job.

That's why product and user understanding sit at the centre of how we work. An engineer who knows our clients' workflows can point agents at the right problem and spot when the result is subtly wrong. Without that, agents just build the wrong thing faster.

Your part is the AI development harness that makes this safe. That means sandboxed environments with synthetic data, scoped and audited access to logs and alerts, and evals and validation gates in CI. It also means firm lines, enforced by tooling, that keep production deploys and secrets in human hands, and client data out of reach of development agents.

You'll also build the agent orchestration pipelines that run in three places: in how we build software, in AI workflows inside the product our clients use, and in the internal tools our implementation team uses to onboard and configure clients.

What you'll do

Build the machine that builds the product

Most of your time goes here.

- Build our AI development harness. Self-service infrastructure, a reproducible development environment, and the sandboxes, guardrails and evals that let agents take on more of the work safely, with results we can measure.

- Automate quality. Build the QA automation pipeline: automated tests, validation gates and release checks that give us confidence in every change, including the ones agents write.

- Orchestrate agents across the business. Build pipelines that run agents reliably and safely in our product workflows and our internal implementation tools, not just in engineering.

Own the platform

- Own our infrastructure. We're migrating to ECS. You'll strengthen our ECS architecture, see the move through in safe, reversible stages, bring every resource under infrastructure as code, and retire the old deployment model.

- Build security into the platform. Tenant-scoped credentials, per-tenant secrets, least-privilege access, and the audit trail that SOC 2 and our clients' security teams expect.

- Make production observable. Set up the monitoring, alerting and tracing we rely on, and build playbooks for on-call and incident response which is shared amongst the team.

Work across the stack

- Make the application changes the harness needs, such as synthetic data, test hooks and the specs agents work from.

- Ship product. Pick up application work in TypeScript and React alongside the team. Over time, you'll learn the codebase as well as the platform it runs on.

- Grow the team around you. Write the design notes and runbooks, pair with and review the work of other engineers, and mentor those who want to grow into infrastructure, so the platform never depends on one person.

Your first six months

- Get the first parts of "the machine" running, and show that they make the team faster without lowering quality.

- At the moment all of our end to end testing is done manually by our Product team. That's a massive manual overhead that bottlenecks our product development. You'll help build our AI-powered QA automation pipeline, so every change, whether a person or an agent wrote it, is tested automatically before it reaches clients.

- Strengthen the ECS architecture and complete the move with no disruption to clients.

- Get the platform fully into code, with tenant isolation and least privilege designed in.

- Put in place the monitoring and on-call foundations the team will build on.

How you'll work

You'll own this area rather than work through a ticket queue. You'll decide what to build and when it's good enough, write your decisions down so others can challenge them, and tell us when something isn't worth doing. You'll work closely with Product from the start of significant work, because the platform exists to serve clients and the engineers building for them.

You and I will work together every day. We'll shape the technical direction together and think through the hard calls, and you'll have a direct line to every decision that affects your work. I'll back your judgement, and I'll expect you to push back when you think I'm wrong.

This is an individual contributor role, but we expect you to multiply the team: leading different areas at different times, and delivering through others as well as through your own work.

You'll probably enjoy this if

- You'd rather build a platform properly than keep patching one.

- You're product-minded. You've probably worked at a startup or scale-up, or even founded something yourself. Seeing your work out in the world, solving real problems, is what motivates you. You ask who a change is for before you ask how to build it.

- You already work this way. Agents write much of your code, and your time goes on design, specs and judging the output. You've built AI tooling for yourself, and probably for others on your team.

- You get satisfaction from making other engineers faster.

- You're comfortable writing Terraform, an API endpoint and an answer to a client's security questionnaire in the same week.

- You've been the person others come to with hard problems, and you've changed your mind publicly when the evidence said so.

This probably isn't for you if

- You want a pure DevOps or SRE role.

- You want to manage people right now. These opportunities might exist in the future, but for now we're small, lean and as flat as possible.

What you'll bring

Very few people match every line. If most of this describes you, we'd like to hear from you.

- Deep, hands-on AWS. Several years running production workloads on ECS or EKS, with a solid grasp of IAM, networking and Lambda.

- Infrastructure as code as a habit , with Terraform or CloudFormation, including bringing existing hand-built resources under code.

- Scaling distributed systems. You've taken systems through real growth in load and data, and can teach others what you learnt.

- Single-tenant SaaS experience. You know the isolation trade-offs and how to keep one client's data and credentials away from another's.

- Security and compliance as part of engineering: least privilege, secrets management, and evidence for SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

- Production experience: on-call, incidents, post-mortems, and observability tooling such as Datadog, Grafana or Honeycomb.

- Full-stack product building. Senior TypeScript and Node.js, plus React, with a track record of shipping features end to end yourself, not just supporting the people who do.

- Test automation and CI/CD. You've designed pipelines that test at the right levels and release safely, and you keep them fast and simple.

- Tooling you've built for AI agents , not just used: agent configuration and orchestration, MCP servers or similar integrations, evals, automated review.

Our stack

TypeScript, Node.js, React and MongoDB Atlas, running on AWS. CircleCI and Bitbucket. AI coding agents are part of everyday work. You don't need experience of all of these.

How we hire

We want to see how you actually work, so there are no whiteboard puzzles.

- Screening call with me (20 minutes)

- Competencies interview with me (30 minutes)

- Technical deep dive with a few of our engineers (90 minutes)

- Culture fit interview with our CEO, Hemal (30 minutes)

I'll be your main point of contact throughout. You'll know what to expect before each stage, and if we don't make an offer, I'll give you feedback.

What You Bring

title: Product Engineer | Design Engineering Knowledge
description:
Product Engineer | Design Engineering Knowledge

Location: Cambridge (UK), hybrid with up to 2 remote days per week

Team: Product

Start date: ASAP

About Neural Concept

Neural Concept is the engineering intelligence platform used by leading manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, and energy. We combine geometric and physics AI with LLM-based agents so engineering teams can move from customer requirements to validated designs in a fraction of the usual time.

About the role

Design decisions depend on information that lives outside the CAD model: customer requirements, design rules, manufacturing and assembly constraints, and cost targets. This information is spread across specification documents, handbooks, ERP systems, requirements management tools, and system models. Engineers gather it by hand, often late in the process, and conflicts surface at design reviews or on the production line.

We call the capability that closes this gap Design Engineering Knowledge. It connects the design to the information ecosystem around it, so requirements, constraints, and trade-offs are available to engineers and AI agents while they work on the design itself.

As a Product Engineer, you will build this capability. Requirements are the first focus area: extracting them from customer specifications and requirements management systems, structuring them, and keeping them traceable. You will then extend the same foundation to design rule checks, Design for Manufacturing (DfM), Design for Assembly (DfA), and Design for Cost, and connect it to the enterprise systems where this knowledge already lives.

You will work with the Product Manager, solution engineers, and customer engineering teams, as the primary developer from the first customer conversation to the version running in production.

What you will do

- Build the requirements foundation: ingest customer specifications and RFQ packages, extract requirements with LLM and agent-based pipelines, and keep each one traceable to its source document and page.

- Extend this foundation to design rules, DfM, DfA, and Design for Cost, turning standards, handbooks, and company know-how into constraints that software and agents can use.

- Bring requirements, constraints, and trade-offs into the design workflow, so engineers can check a design against them at any stage and see which ones apply to the part they are working on.

- Build integrations with the systems around the design: requirements management systems, ERP (cost, materials, and supplier data), and system design and MBSE tools for architecture and system-level requirements.

- Design the data model that links requirements, rules, and constraints to parts, design parameters, and simulation results.

- Create evaluation sets and quality metrics with customers, so extraction and checking accuracy is measured and improves with every release.

- Design human-in-the-loop review flows where engineers validate and edit AI output, with versioning and a full audit trail.

- Spot recurring patterns across customers and turn them into reusable components of the Neural Concept platform.

Who you are

Must have

- Experience building and shipping production Python software in fast-moving, cross-functional teams.

- Hands-on experience with LLM applications in production: structured outputs, retrieval-augmented generation, agents, and evaluation.

- Experience integrating with enterprise systems through APIs and data models, for example ERP, PLM, or requirements management tools.

- Experience with document processing, such as PDF parsing, OCR, or information extraction.

- Strong software practices: testing (pytest), CI, packaging, code review, and git.

- A product mindset. You talk to users, understand the problem before writing code, and ship in small, measurable steps.

- Clear, concise communication with both customer engineers and internal teams.

- Based in Cambridge (UK) or willing to relocate.

Nice to have

- Background in mechanical engineering or physics, with exposure to DfM, DfA, or design-to-cost practices.

- Familiarity with requirements engineering and model-based systems engineering (MBSE, SysML).

- Experience working with CAD data or geometry processing.

- Experience with vision-language models, vector databases, or search ranking.

What you get

- Ownership of a product capability that customers use in real engineering programs, with direct access to the engineers who use it.

- A competitive salary and rewarding opportunities as we continue to scale.

- A collaborative, multicultural team where your work is visible and recognized.

- Colleagues who share knowledge freely and support each other.

- A hybrid model and flexible hours. We focus on results and trust you to organize your time.

We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and we're committed to building a diverse and inclusive environment where you can thrive.

description:

About Bike Club

Bike Club is looking for a fractional Product Lead to lead the member product, turn customer needs and commercial priorities into a clear direction and a prioritised roadmap, and deliver measurable improvements. The role combines senior Product leadership with practical discovery and delivery coordination in a lean team.

The Product Lead will also establish an AI-enabled Product function, using AI to speed up customer insight, discovery, prototyping and experimentation. They will identify where AI and automation can improve the member experience or business efficiency, and turn the strongest opportunities into prioritised, measurable initiatives.

This is a part-time fixed-term employment or freelance contract estimated at 3 days per week for a period of 3 months.

Key Responsibilities 

- Product direction and roadmap: own the direction and roadmap across the member lifecycle: joining, managing a subscription, ongoing membership, exchange and retention. Balance member value with operational efficiency, cost and business priorities.

- Discovery: lead discovery with members and colleagues across Marketing, Customer Service, Operations and markets. Use research, behavioural data and service insight to define problems before committing to solutions.

- Lifecycle and retention: work jointly with Marketing and the retention owner on lifecycle journeys, retention initiatives, experiments and shared measures. Product owns the supporting experience and requirements. Marketing owns campaign and channel execution.

- Requirements and backlog: turn agreed priorities into clear requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria. Maintain one prioritised product backlog, including operational improvements and approved AI or automation initiatives.

- Investment cases: build proportionate cases for investment, setting out expected benefits, cost, dependencies and how outcomes will be measured. Recommend stopping or deferring work where value is insufficient.

- Delivery: agree delivery commitments with Engineering using realistic estimates and available capacity. Coordinate stakeholders, adoption and launches with the combined QA and Delivery role, keeping risks and changes visible.

- Marketing autonomy: support Marketing with appropriate content, landing-page and experimentation capabilities. Agree the boundary between the member product, CRM and support tools.

- AI in Product work: use AI routinely for research synthesis, analysis, requirements development, prototyping and experiment design, and validate findings against customer evidence.

- Prioritise valuable applications with Marketing, Customer Service, Operations and the Data and Automation function. Test assumptions and build proportionate business cases. Customer-service automation should support the wider member journey.

- Share responsibility with Marketing for using AI to support lifecycle insight, proposition testing and retention experiments, with agreed measures of customer and commercial impact.

- Leave things in a better state: because the engagement is part-time and time-limited, document the roadmap, backlog, ways of working and AI approach so the team can continue without the Product Lead, and hand over clearly at the end.

Requirements 

- Extensive Product Management experience including owning a digital product roadmap and delivering measurable customer and commercial improvements, preferably in a subscription, membership or related consumer business.

- Strong discovery skills, including customer interviews, journey mapping, data interpretation, problem definition and testing assumptions before investment.

- Commercial judgement: can compare value, effort, cost and risk, build practical investment cases and make clear prioritisation decisions.

- Ability to lead across functions, challenge senior stakeholders constructively and maintain focus when priorities compete.

- Experience working with Engineering, Design, Marketing, Customer Service and Operations through delivery, launch and continuous improvement.

- Demonstrable experience embedding AI into Product workflows, with examples of faster learning, better decisions or reduced effort. Able to distinguish valuable AI applications from features that add unnecessary complexity.

- Track record of working independently and effectively in a part-time, fractional or interim capacity, making visible progress in limited days a week.

- Able to start quickly, and leave behind clear documentation and repeatable ways of working.

Measures Of Success 

Baselines, numerical targets, data sources and review dates are agreed with the executive sponsor and relevant business owners within the first 30 days. Delivery and outcomes are reviewed weekly.

- Member retention: improvement in the agreed retention or cancellation measure for targeted journeys, assessed jointly with Marketing and the retention owner.

- Member experience: improvement in self-service completion and reduction in avoidable support contact for prioritised journeys, without deterioration in customer experience.

- Conversion: improvement in agreed joining and exchange conversion measures, using experiments or comparable cohorts where practical.

- Speed of learning: reduced time from identifying a customer problem to testing a solution, with evidence that decisions remain grounded in customer insight.

- AI and automation: validated initiatives deliver agreed improvements in member experience, retention or operational efficiency, measured with the relevant business owner.

- Roadmap value: proportion of priority initiatives with a stated outcome, baseline and measurement plan before delivery, followed by a documented benefits review.

- Delivery confidence: performance against jointly agreed milestones, with changes in scope, priorities and dependencies recorded and communicated early.

Our Values 

We look for people who live our values every day: 

Ease: we make things simple for our members and for each other. 

Care: we look after our customers, our colleagues and our bikes. 

Progress: we keep improving, learning and raising the bar. 

Joy: we help kids fall in love with cycling, and enjoy the work we do. 

Why Bike Club? 

You'll be joining a business with a clear purpose, a genuinely different proposition and significant opportunity to grow.

This is a rare opportunity to build the operating system for our national refurbishment and distribution site from the ground up, shaping how Bike Club gets the right bike to every family, right when they need it.

- 3–5 years in renewals, account management, or a customer-facing sales role with upsell and cross-sell closing experience, ideally in SaaS or cybersecurity.

- A track record of hitting or beating quota, including driving net revenue retention above 100% on your own book, with expansion outpacing churn rather than renewal completion alone.

- Proven experience running consultative upsell and cross-sell motions, identifying and closing whitespace within an existing customer base, and negotiating confidently with senior and economic buyers across multi-stakeholder conversations.

- A risk-aware instinct for spotting early signals of churn or downgrade, combined with strong forecasting discipline, CRM hygiene, and hands-on experience with Salesforce and CPQ or quoting tools.

- Strong communication and organizational skills, curiosity about customer use cases and the product, and a habit of opening expansion conversations unprompted, with comfort in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. Exposure to Channel/MSSP or 2-tier GTM models is a plus.

Livestorm is the world's leading end-to-end video engagement platform. Founded in 2016, Livestorm allows companies to organize powerful online meetings, webinars and virtual events from end-to-end. - Stay curious: Be interested in the world around you.

- Be resourceful: Go that extra mile in the most efficient way.

MISSION 

Livestorm sales team is a team of entrepreneurial and driven sales professionals. They are playing a key role in the expansion of Livestorm as we establish ourselves as a market leader in the video communication market, leveraging Livestorm's existing customer references, marketing programs, turning leads into long-lasting partnerships.

Account Executives are responsible for identifying, segmenting, engaging, and converting qualified Mid-Market and Enterprise prospects into paying customers according to an annual quota.

You will report to the Head of New Business, and will closely collaborate with all our teams (Marketing, Sales, Customer Care, Product and Finance) to drive maximum value and success with new Livestorm customers.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL 

- Qualify inbound marketing source leads (MQLs) coming from Mid-Market & Enterprise prospects and turn them, if qualified, into opportunities and closed contracts

- Focus your outbound efforts on the Enterprise segment (with a focus on the Finance, Healthcare & Tech industries ) and develop / execute sales strategies and tactics to generate pipeline, drive sales opportunities and deliver repeatable and predictable bookings

- Work on the NEMEA (Nordics & UK) and US market (native speakers are preferred for this role / previous sales experience in these regions is a big plus). 

- Use of a variety of channels to identify new prospects and close new deals such as social media, internet, web-based tools & outbound calling

- Manage effectively all CRM activity relating to your accounts (Salesforce) and all the tech stack of an AE at Livestorm (SalesNav, Salesloft, Modjo, Chili Piper, Notion & more)

- Pro-actively work with other teams (Account Management, Growth & Marketing, Customer Success, etc.)

- Provide clients’ feedback, especially on product, in order for Livestorm to adjust and prioritize its product roadmap.

At Livestorm, we believe that diversity's got talent! We are committed to building an inclusive company culture in which a diverse mix of talented people will feel proud to join and engage. Our goal is to ensure that every Stormie feels valued and has the opportunity to thrive. Ready to apply? We are ready to meet you! All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. 

JOB REQUIREMENTS 

- Experienced: You have extensive experience (+3 years minimum) of successfully selling Software/SaaS license agreements into Enterprise / Large accounts in France and abroad across a variety of industries (expertise in the Finance & Healthcare industries is a plus)

- Industry Knowledge: A good understanding of selling video communication platform would be ideal however, a background in selling SaaS and closing 6/7 figure deals is more important

- Overachiever: You have consistently achieved and/or exceeded your sales goals across your geographic territory and have a track record in closing 6/7 figure contracts - You are results oriented

- Outbound Mindset: You have a desire, even an obsession, to identify new prospects, contacts and decision makers to expand the number of new logos

- Excellent Communication: You know what to say (both internally and with clients) and more importantly, how to say it in both French and English

- Collaborator : You know that selling is a team sport and will partner with virtual teams to ensure success. You have experience in working with remote teams and clients to close joint business

- Go-Getter: Willing to go the extra mile with a strong work ethic - disciplined and resourceful.

Moreover, we are looking for someone based in Paris (to meet prospects, go on events and be close to your management) but working remotely anywhere in France is permitted. 

Confidence can sometimes hold us back from applying for a job. But we'll let you in on a secret: there's no such thing as a 'perfect' candidate. So however you identify and whatever background you bring with you, please apply if this is a role that would make you excited to come into work every day.

title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
About Payflows 

At Payflows, we build software that helps large companies manage and automate their payment workflows. It’s not the flashiest part of a business, but it’s one of the most critical: invoices, approvals, payments, and controls. When these things slow down, the whole company feels it. 

But our ambition goes further than just building a better workflow tool. 

We believe the future of finance operations is not faster clicking: it’s no clicking at all 🫳 🎤 

Finance teams shouldn’t spend their days moving data from one screen to another. Software should do the operational work, and humans should focus on reviewing, approving, and making the decisions that matter. 

That’s the direction we’re building toward: an agent-driven finance platform , where intelligent agents handle the repetitive tasks, and users stay in control. 

We started in 2022 with a small team and a rough first version of the product. Three years later, we’re working with major companies across France, the UK, and the US while choosing to keep our team small and human-sized. 

We moved fast, shipped a lot, and not everything was built in a perfect way. But it helped us learn quickly, sign real customers, and prove that the problem we’re solving truly matters. 

In 2024, investors trusted us with a $25M Series A. That gives us the chance to keep growing while also strengthening our foundations and building the system that will power this agent-driven future. 

Today, we’re about 35 people from many different countries, and we’re looking for a few amazing humans to join the next chapter. 🤗 

🚀 What you’ll actually do 

You’ll help build a product that real finance teams rely on every day. 

For us, engineering is not just about clean code, it’s about reliability, clarity, and trust, especially when money and automation are involved. 

In a typical week, you might: 

- Design and implement new services for a product feature. 

- Refactor an early service to make it more robust. 

- Investigate a performance or production issue. 

- Work with product and frontend to shape a new feature. 

- Review code and help teammates improve. 

- Build backend tools that our AI agents use to perform real finance operations. 

- Design safe, deterministic workflows where agents propose actions and humans review them. 

Your time will be split between building new features and improving what already exists . Both matter. 

You won’t just build endpoints. You’ll help shape the execution layer that our agents rely on: the APIs, data models, and workflows that let them act safely in production. 

You’ll work closely with product, frontend, and customer-facing teams. We expect engineers to take ownership of parts of the system and help make them more reliable over time. 

💻 Our current tech reality 

Our stack evolves based on our challenges, but we care more about good design than trendy tools 🙏 

Python is our core language. It helps us move fast, keep the code readable, and fits naturally with our AI-driven approach. A growing part of the system is built around agents that use our backend as a set of reliable, deterministic tools. 

- Core language: Python 

- Backend: FastAPI + Pydantic 

- Data: PostgreSQL 

- Infra: AWS, serverless when it makes sense 

- Performance: some Rust for critical paths 

- Architecture: multi-service backend, simple enough to reason about 

Some parts of the system are clean and well-tested. Others were built quickly and need love. That’s the phase we’re in. 

Over the next year, we’ll focus on: 

- Turning core workflows into reliable tools for our agents 

- Simplifying services 

- Improving tests and observability 

- Making performance more predictable 

- Cleaning up early code 

We know we’re not perfect, but we care a lot about improving step by step. 

✨ Who’s going to thrive with us 

You’ll probably feel comfortable here if: 

- You like building products people actually use. 

- You are autonomous and take ownership of what you ship. 

- You take initiative and lead by example. 

- You’re curious and enjoy figuring things out. 

- You’re pragmatic about trade-offs. 

- You communicate with kindness and clarity. 

This role is a great fit if you’re excited by the idea of: 

- Building systems that are used by AI agents, not just humans. 

- Designing reliable, safe automation in production. 

- Working on a product that is still early and evolving quickly. 

You don’t need to know everything about AI. But you should be curious about it and excited to work in a system where agents are part of the core product 🤖 

🧩 What you’ll get from this role 

- Real ownership over parts of the system. 

- Direct impact on customers and product decisions. 

- A small, human team where your work is visible and meaningful 🤝 

- A mix of feature work, system design, and technical improvements. 

- Exposure to real scaling and production challenges. 

- The chance to help build an agent-driven product from the inside. 

We offer: 

- Competitive salary and equity. 

- Flexible remote setup (we prefer people to come into Paris or London office twice per week. At a minimum we’d ask you to be at an office 3 days per month, onboard in Paris for your first few weeks, and work CEST timezone). 

- A high-autonomy environment where you have real ownership and space to make an impact. 

- Plenty of room to grow, take responsibility, and shape parts of the product. 

- A culture based on trust, ownership, and clear communication. 

This isn’t a huge corporate environment. In exchange, you get autonomy, responsibility, and the chance to shape a product that’s still early in its story—and help build what finance operations will look like in the next decade 🚀

title: DevOps / Infra Lead
description:
🌍 Our Vision & Mission 

At Payflows, we give finance teams the tools to reclaim their time and energy. Our platform weaves together banking connectivity, payments, AI, and procurement so they can ditch the busywork and focus on what really moves the needle. 

🤝 Why Join Us? 

We’re a small, mighty team who’ve earned our stripes at Airbnb, Luko, BNP Paribas, and Facebook. It’s not always easy—things move fast, and we expect a lot—but if you’re hungry for impact, you’ll find it here.

🚀 What You’ll Do 

You'll own the infrastructure for a product that real finance teams rely on every day.

For us, infrastructure is not just about uptime; it's about reliability, security, and trust - especially when money and automation are involved. The platform has to be boring in the best possible way: predictable, observable, and safe to deploy to.

- In a typical week, you might:

- Evolve our infrastructure-as-code to add a service, a queue, or a whole new environment.

- Improve our CI/CD pipelines so engineers ship safely and fast, dozens of times a day.

- Investigate a production issue: a latency spike, a failing deploy, a database under load.

- Strengthen observability with dashboards, alerts, and traces, so we catch problems before customers do.

- Harden our security, secrets management, and access controls.

- Tune cost and performance across our AWS footprint.

Your time will be split between building new platform capabilities and making what already exists more reliable . Both matter.

You'll help shape the foundation that everything else stands on: the pipelines, environments, and guardrails that let engineers and our AI agents act safely in production.

You'll work closely with backend, frontend, and the AI team. We expect you to take ownership of the platform and make it more reliable over time, not wait for tickets.

💻 Our current tech reality 

Our stack evolves based on our challenges, but we care more about good design than trendy tools 

We're an AWS shop, and we lean on managed services and infrastructure-as-code so the system is reproducible and easy to reason with. A growing part of our world is making the backend a set of reliable, deterministic tools that AI agents can call, which raises the bar on reliability even further.

- Cloud: AWS

- Infra-as-code: Pulumi (Python)

- Compute: ECS + Lambda, serverless when it makes sense

- Data: PostgreSQL on RDS/Aurora

- CI/CD: GitLab CI

- Orchestration: Airflow (MWAA)

- Observability: Grafana Cloud, CloudWatch, Sentry

- Auth & identity: Cognito, IAM

- Edge & frontend: API Gateway, ALB, AWS Amplify for the web app

Some of this is clean, version-controlled, and reproducible. Other parts grew fast and live a little too much in people’s heads instead of in code. Closing that gap is a big part of why this role exists.

Over the next year, we'll focus on:

- Making every environment reproducible from code

- Better observability and alerting, fewer surprises

- Tightening the security and compliance posture that comes with handling enterprise finance data

- Faster, safer deploys

- Keeping AWS costs sane as we scale

🧑‍💻 What we’re looking for 

- 5+ years of experience with Python or any other OOP language 

- Backend expertise : APIs, microservices, architecture best practices 

- Databases & SQL : Data modeling, query optimization 

- Git lover : Comfortable with version control and code reviews 

- Pragmatic engineering mindset : Build, test, refine, simplify—smart shortcuts when time is tight 

🧩 Bonus points if you’ve worked on: 

- B2B SaaS or finance/ERP tools 

- BaaS APIs or payment infra 

- Serverless, AWS, event-driven architecture exposure 

✨ Who's going to thrive with us 

You'll probably feel comfortable here if: 

- You think in systems and instinctively automate yourself out of repetitive work.

- You treat infrastructure as code, not as pets.

- You stay calm during incidents and are genuinely good at root-causing.

- You care about security, because you're handling other people's money.

- You are autonomous and take ownership of what you ship.

- You take initiative and lead by example.

- You're pragmatic about trade-offs.

- You communicate with kindness and clarity.

You don't need to know everything about AI - but you must be curious about it and excited to build the reliable foundation that agents run on 🤖

🧩 What you'll get from this role 

- Real ownership over the platform the whole company runs on.

- Direct impact on reliability, security, and how fast every engineer can ship.

- A mix of platform building, system design, and reliability work.

- Exposure to real scaling and production challenges.

- The chance to help build the foundation of an agent-driven product from the inside.

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 

About the role 

You are BLP's first in-house lawyer. You build the legal function from scratch and protect a business that puts agentic AI into the ERP processes of 550+ enterprise customers. You report to the CFO and partner closely with Sales, Finance, People and Product, covering four entities in Switzerland, Germany, the UK and the US, with customers in 40+ countries. In your first 12 months, Sales runs on your contract playbook and standard templates, and BLP has a clear compliance framework for data protection and AI regulation.

What you'll do 

· Own commercial contracting end-to-end: negotiate customer MSAs, DPAs and SLAs with enterprise procurement and legal teams, so deals close faster with risk you can explain to the CFO.

· Build the legal toolkit: templates, a negotiation playbook with fallback positions and clear approval rules, so Sales can handle standard deals without escalating to you.

· Lead data protection and AI compliance across GDPR, the Swiss FADP and the EU AI Act, and support security reviews and certifications, so enterprise customers trust how we handle their data.

· Run corporate housekeeping for BLP Digital AG and its subsidiaries in Germany, the UK and the US: board and shareholder matters and cap table

· Advise on employment law across our countries and protect our IP and trademarks, working with the People team on contracts, policies and equity plans.

· Select and manage external counsel, deciding what stays in-house and what goes out.

What you'll bring 

· You bring 7+ years of legal experience, including at least 3 years in-house at a B2B SaaS or tech company, ideally after training at a leading law firm.

· You are admitted to the bar in Switzerland or another European jurisdiction and are comfortable advising on Swiss, EU, UK and US matters with appropriate external support.

· You have personally negotiated enterprise SaaS contracts with large corporate customers and closed them on terms the business could live with.

· You have hands-on GDPR and data protection experience and follow the EU AI Act closely.

· You have built something from zero before: a template library, a contract process or a legal function, and you are happy to be the only lawyer in the room.

· You are pragmatic and commercial in your approach. You give clear, risk-weighted advice in plain language, at the speed of a fast-growing company, in fluent English and German language.

Strong plus 

· Experience with venture financing rounds, ESOP setups and/or M&A.

· Background in ERP, finance automation or AI products.

· Experience with ISO 27001 or SOC 2 audits from the legal side.

What you'll get 

· Founding ownership. You shape BLP's legal function from day one and decide how it scales.

· Direct line to leadership. You report directly to the CFO and work with the leadership team on decisions that matter.

· Global scope. Four entities, 40+ countries and enterprise customers give you breadth few in-house roles offer.

· You work at the front line of AI regulation, applied to real enterprise processes.

· You grow with the company and are set up to build and lead a team as legal needs expand.

· You work from our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, with a team that values Impact, Transparency, Ownership and Excellence.

· Competitive package. 

Learn more about BLP and our values at blp.digital/company/careers .

title: Strategic Account Executive (Zurich)
description:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

ROLE OVERVIEW 

We are seeking a motivated and results-driven Strategic Account Executive to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for driving new business within your territory, focusing on building and maintaining strong relationships with key stakeholders across various personas within an account. You will play a crucial role in expanding our customer base and ensuring successful sales outcomes through effective pipeline generation and accurate sales forecasting.

RESPONSIBILITIES 

- Pipeline Generation: Creating 80% of your pipeline by identifying new business opportunities and engaging with multiple personas within the prospect/customer base. Utilize various strategies and tools to generate leads and move them through the sales cycle.

- Sales Forecasting: Develop and maintain accurate sales forecasts (+/- 10 of goal), leveraging data to inform decision-making and ensure predictable revenue outcomes with the goal of consistent attainment of revenue targets.

- Solution Selling: Effectively communicate the value of our platform, tailoring presentations and proposals to meet the specific needs of each prospect.

- Negotiation and Closing: Lead negotiations with potential clients, by thoughtfully addressing key stakeholders including multiple personas and CxO in the buyer journey, while navigating organizational complexities, addressing objections and securing new business agreements.

- Account Management: Work across multiple personas within an account to understand their unique needs and align Benchling’s solutions with their business objectives.

- Collaboration: Partner with internal teams (marketing, product, customer success, etc) and Channel to ensure a seamless experience for clients and drive long-term customer satisfaction.

- Continuous Learning: Stay informed about industry trends, competitors, and emerging technologies to maintain a competitive edge in the market.

- Process: Drive the sales process through Pipeline Generation (PG), 3 Why’s, Champion Building, MEDDICC, Command of the Message, etc. Maintain account integrity and opportunity data within company systems; Salesforce.

QUALIFICATIONS 

You are drawn to our mission and you want to help Benchling win new business. You are committed to working in a collaborative environment, working together as a team. You have a love for working in a fast-paced environment and taking the initiative to get stuff done and try new things. You are passionate about powering new possibilities in biotech faster.

- Proven experience as an Account Executive, preferably within a data management, workflow SaaS or technology-driven environment that sells to multiple personas across IT & Line of business.

- Demonstrated ability to drive pipeline generation and manage complex sales cycles.

- Strong sales forecasting skills with a track record of meeting or exceeding targets.

- Demonstrated success in selling products or solutions that typically fall outside of pre-established budgets, with a proven ability to build a compelling business case and influence purchasing decisions.

- Experience working with diverse personas within an account (from technical decision makers, business decision makers & CxO execs), with the ability to influence decision-making at all the levels.

- Dynamic communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.

- Self-motivated, with a strong drive to achieve and exceed goals.

- Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a team environment.

- Familiarity with MEDDICC sales methodology is a plus but not required.

- Knowledge of the life sciences industry, including: R&D, and/or IT functions is preferred but not required.

- Bachelor’s degree - life sciences major is preferred but not required.

HOW WE WORK

We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

#BI-Hybrid #BI-Remote

The qualifications you need:

- Domain & Industry: Deep understanding of the Finance/Supply Chain domains. You stay continuously updated on business-critical use cases.

- Degree: Engineering, Computer Science, Mathematics, Business Analytics, comparable technical degree or a Business/Economics degree paired with a technical minor

What Celonis can offer you:

- Ownership from Day 1: Every full-time "Celonaut" is an owner, receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and merit-based refresh grants.

- Work-Life Integration: Enjoy Unlimited PTO (in applicable regions) and generous PTO globally, as well as a flexible hybrid work model that balances remote focus with vibrant office collaboration.

- Holistic Well-being: Prioritize your health with subsidized Wellhub memberships, mental health counseling, and dedicated "Wellness Weeks" that prioritize work/life balance.

- Drive Sustainability: Participate in annual Impact Days, where you receive paid time off to volunteer for community and environmental causes with your local office, or virtually.

- Global Inclusion & Belonging: Find community through our Inclusion Think Tank and participate in our annual Inclusion Days, ensuring every voice is heard and valued.

- Value-Driven Impact: Join a mission-led organization where our core values—Live for Customer Value, The Best Team Wins, We Own It, and Earth Is Our Future—drive every decision.

About Us: 

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI, empowering organizations to analyze, design, and operate AI-driven processes. The Celonis Platform is powered by the Celonis Context Model, which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence to create a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can understand — turning AI’s operational blind spots into operational clarity. Industry-leading companies around the world trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. title: Senior Specialist, QA
description:
About Summit: 

Summit Therapeutics Inc. is a biopharmaceutical oncology company with a mission focused on improving quality of life, increasing potential duration of life, and resolving serious unmet medical needs. At Summit, we believe in building a team of world class professionals who are passionate about this mission, and it is our people who drive this mission to reality. Summit’s core values include integrity, passion for excellence, purposeful urgency, collaboration, and our commitment to people. Our employees are truly the heart and soul of our culture, and they are invaluable in shaping our journey toward excellence.

Summit’s team is inspired to touch and help change lives through Summit’s clinical studies in the field of oncology. Summit has multiple global Phase 3 clinical studies, including:

Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) 

- 
HARMONi: Phase 3 clinical study which was intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to placebo plus chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC who were previously treated with a 3rd generation EGFR TKI.

- 
HARMONi-3: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy compared to pembrolizumab combined with chemotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

- 
HARMONi-7: Phase 3 clinical study which is intended to evaluate ivonescimab monotherapy compared to pembrolizumab monotherapy in patients with first-line metastatic NSCLC.

Colorectal Cancer (CRC) 

- 
HARMONi-GI3: Phase 3 clinical study intended to evaluate ivonescimab in combination with chemotherapy compared with bevacizumab plus chemotherapy.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy not presently approved by any regulatory authority other than China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Summit is headquartered in Miami, Florida, and has additional offices in California, New Jersey, the UK, and Ireland. 

Overview of Role: 

The Senior Specialist, QA will provide operational leadership and quality oversight for the review, approval and release-readiness of clinical and commercial product batches. 

The role is responsible for ensuring that batch documentation is complete, accurate, traceable, and compliant with applicable GMP requirements, approved procedures and regulatory commitments before submission to QA for final disposition or QP certification. The person will coordinate batch-release activities across Quality, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs and external manufacturing partners, ensuring that issues are identified, escalated and resolved in a timely manner. The position will also lead process improvements, support inspection readiness and promote high standards of data integrity and Good Documentation Practice across the batch-release process. 

Key Responsibilities 

- Batch Review and Release Readiness 

- Coordinate the end-to-end QA review of executed batch manufacturing, packaging, testing and release documentation for IMP and Commercial biological batch records. 

- Coordinate the preparation and collation of batch documentation required for final batch disposition or QP certification from internal and external sources. 

- Verify that batch records are complete, accurate, and compliant with approved procedures, specifications and applicable GMP requirements. 

- Confirm that relevant deviations, investigations, change controls, CAPAs, and laboratory results have been appropriately assessed and approved before release. 

- Identify documentation gaps, discrepancies and potential compliance risks, and coordinate their timely resolution. 

- Maintain oversight of batch-release priorities, review status, outstanding actions, and planned release dates. 

- Escalate critical issues or potential delays to Quality leadership and relevant stakeholders. 

- Ensure that batch-release documentation is appropriately archived and readily retrievable electronically. 

- Quality Systems and Compliance: 

- Ensure batch-release activities are performed in accordance with current GMP, Good Documentation Practice, data-integrity principles, and internal procedures. 

- Support the effective operation of quality systems associated with deviations, CAPAs, change controls, document control, and training. 

- Review and approve relevant quality documents, including SOPs, work instructions, forms, checklists, and batch-release procedures. 

- Maintain controlled documentation and ensure that current approved versions are available to relevant personnel. 

- Support periodic reviews of procedures and identify opportunities to strengthen compliance and operational effectiveness. 

- Promote the appropriate use of electronic quality and document management systems. 

- Act as a subject-matter expert for batch documentation, release-readiness and associated document-control processes for all batch release activities. 

- Internal Team Coordination (EU QA) 

- Provide day-to-day leadership and technical guidance to QA batch reviewers and supporting personnel. 

- Plan and allocate batch-review activities according to business priorities, product demand, and release timelines. 

- Monitor team workload, quality metrics, and completion of assigned activities. 

- Develop and deliver training in Good Documentation Practice, batch-record review and relevant quality-system processes. 

- Support onboarding and qualifications of new QA team members. 

- Foster a collaborative, accountable, and continuous-improvement culture within the QA function. 

- External Team Collaboration: 

- Work closely with Manufacturing, Quality Control / CMC, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Supply and other relevant functions to support timely batch release. 

- Coordinate with all Summit CMOs, testing laboratories and service providers to obtain missing documents and resolve release-related queries. 

- Communicate batch status, risks, priorities and outstanding actions clearly to internal and external stakeholders. 

- Support changes affecting batch documentation or release processes. 

- Participate in cross-functional meetings concerning batch disposition, documentation, readiness, and supply continuity internally. 

- Inspection Readiness and Continuous Improvement 

- Maintain batch-release processes and supporting records in a continuous state of inspection of readiness. 

- Support regulatory inspections, customer audits, internal audits, and supplier audits. 

- Retrieve and present batch documentation and quality-system records during audits and inspections. 

- Track batch-review metrics, recurring documentation issues, cycle times, and overdue actions. 

- Analyse trends and recommend improvements to increase efficiency, right-first-time performance and compliance. 

- Lead or contribute to Lean and process-optimization initiatives within the batch-release function. 

- Support the implementation and enhancement of electronic quality, document management and reporting systems. 

Qualifications and Experience 

- Essential 

- Recognized qualification in Quality, Pharmaceutical Science, Life Sciences, Engineering or related discipline. 

- Significant experience in Quality Assurance within a pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical or similarly regulated manufacturing environment – preferably in Biologic manufacturing, Packaging and Labelling environments. 

- Practical experience reviewing executed batch records and supporting batch disposition or QP certification activities. 

- Knowledge of GMP, Good Documentation Practice, and data-integrity requirements. 

- Experience working with deviations, investigations, CAPAs, and change controls. 

- Experience using electronic quality, document management and other enterprise-systems - systems such as MasterControl, NetSuite, Veeva Vault, TrackWise, SAP or equivalent platforms. 

- Demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple priorities and deliver against critical release timelines. 

- Experience supporting the release of medicinal products or investigational medicinal products. 

- Experience working with contract manufacturing organizations and external testing laboratories 

- Key Competencies 

- Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy 

- Sound quality and compliance judgement 

- Leadership and team coordination 

- Effective prioritization and workload management 

- Problem-solving and risk-based decision-making 

- Clear communication and stakeholder management 

- Audit and inspection readiness 

- Data integrity and information governance 

- Process improvement and operational efficiency 

- Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment 

Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, depth of experience, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor. The total compensation package for this position may also include bonus, stock, benefits and/or other applicable variable compensation.

title: Systems Engineer
description:
80-100% | as soon as possible | Germany or Switzerland 

About Exeon 

Exeon is a Swiss cyber security company based in Zurich. Since 2016, we have been protecting critical infrastructures, financial institutions and enterprises whose operations fully rely on IT through AI-powered analysis of network communication. This makes the most sophisticated cyberattacks visible – attacks conventional tools fail to detect. We combine Swiss excellence with a flexible, remote-first, and collaborative culture, supporting passionate, ambitious professionals devoted to solving cybersecurity challenges and driving continuous innovation. 

What your impact will be like: 

As a Systems Engineer in our Solutions team, you will help design the components and data flow of our core products: how data gets in, how deployments are configured and operated, and how everything scales across very different customer environments, many of them on-prem and air-gapped. 

You’ll split your time between building (ingestion pipelines, automation, tooling) and deploying and operating (working with customers to get Exeon running reliably in their environments), so your work shapes both scalability and customer success.

In particular, you will:

- Build tooling and automation to simplify the deployment, configuration, and lifecycle management of Exeon.NDR, Exeon.UEBA, log collection and supporting components 

- Design, build, and maintain scalable log ingestion pipelines for a wide range of network and application log sources and formats, including parsing, normalization, and validation 

- Deploy and operate Exeon in customer environments (on-prem, private cloud, and hybrid), including sizing, performance tuning, and troubleshooting complex issues 

- Work with customers to understand their data sources, infrastructure constraints, and security needs, and translate these into clear requirements for product and engineering teams 

- Contribute to customer support, documentation, and runbooks alongside your Solutions colleagues

What you can expect from us: 

Exeon offers an open company culture that values and encourages diversity, teamwork and a growth mindset. Our goal is to provide our employees with an exciting, supportive and motivating environment for personal growth and career development while ensuring that our team maintains a healthy work-life balance. We strive to achieve this by offering:

- An exciting and impactful job in a fast-growing Swiss cyber tech company expanding across Europe with manifold opportunities to shape your professional profile.

- Working in close collaboration with our interdisciplinary team and learning from our Security Experts, Data Scientists, and Business Professionals.

- Taking over responsibilities quickly and help shape and promote a cutting-edge security software.

- A high degree of trust, independence and flexibility, also in terms of working hours and place of work (remote or in the office).

- A competitive salary and appealing benefits package.

What you bring along: 

We are looking for a proactive, self-motivated and enthusiastic cyber security professional who is comfortable in a high-paced start-up environment and who shares our values. You should be confident with solving problems independently and communicating easily with both internal teams and directly with customers. You should also:

- 3-5 years of experience in systems engineering, data engineering, platform/infrastructure engineering, or a similar role 

- Working knowledge of network and application security and the telemetry relevant to detection 

- UNIX/Linux experience, including networking, troubleshooting, and performance tuning in containerized deployments (Docker and/or Kubernetes) 

- Strong programming skills in Python and Bash (or comparable languages), with a focus on automation and maintainable, production-quality code 

- Hands-on experience designing and operating data ingestion pipelines (e.g. syslog, Logstash/Fluentd/Vector, Elastic stack, or similar), including handling heterogeneous formats and high volumes 

- Comfortable with working in a largely remote team where clear communication is key to successful collaboration and impact. We are an English-speaking team but German fluency is appreciated when communicating to some customers 

- Degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

Nice to have:

- Solid understanding of network and application security fundamentals, common attack patterns, and the log and telemetry sources that matter for detection 

- Experience with SIEM, SOAR, or detection platforms (e.g. Splunk, Sentinel, Elastic Security), or as a detection engineer or security analyst 

- Familiarity with network telemetry such as NetFlow/IPFIX, Zeek, or Suricata, and frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK 

- Prior customer-facing or professional services experience.
